#4321. A surprising discovery could help aging muscles repair themselves

Muscles can begin losing their strength and ability to recover surprisingly early in the aging process. Over time, muscle tissue may develop scar tissue, accumulate fat, and lose some of the specialized fibers responsible for rapid, powerful movements. These changes can make everyday activities more difficult and gradually reduce mobility and physical independence.

Now, scientists in Japan have identified a promising molecule that could help protect the body's natural muscle repair system and potentially make it more effective. In laboratory experiments, the compound strengthened an important biological signal involved in muscle regeneration, increasing its ability to connect with a key cellular receptor by more than twofold.

The discovery comes from a team led by Professor Ryuichi Tatsumi at Kyushu University's Faculty of Agriculture. Their findings, published in Scientific Reports, suggest a possible new approach to addressing the cellular changes that make aging muscles increasingly difficult to repair.

How Aging Disrupts the Body's Muscle Repair System

Skeletal muscles are the muscles attached to bones that allow us to walk, lift objects, maintain posture, and perform other voluntary movements. Although these muscles experience wear and tear throughout life, they also have a remarkable ability to repair themselves.

Much of that repair depends on specialized stem cells known as satellite cells. These cells normally remain inactive, positioned alongside muscle fibers until they receive a signal that repair or regeneration is needed. Once activated, they can multiply and develop into muscle cells that help restore damaged tissue.

An essential part of this process involves a protein called hepatocyte growth factor, or HGF. Despite its name, HGF plays important roles beyond the liver, including helping activate the stem cells responsible for muscle regeneration.

Under normal conditions, HGF is stored within the supportive material surrounding muscle fibers. When muscles experience an injury or mechanical stimulation, such as physical movement or stretching, the protein can be released.

HGF then attaches to a receptor called c-met on the surface of satellite cells. Receptors are specialized proteins that receive molecular signals and trigger responses inside cells. In this case, the interaction helps awaken dormant satellite cells, allowing them to multiply, mature, and participate in repairing muscle fibers.

But this carefully coordinated system becomes less reliable with age.

A Hidden Chemical Change May Weaken Aging Muscles

The researchers' previous work revealed that HGF can undergo a chemical modification known as nitration. This process attaches a chemical group called a nitro group to particular locations on a protein, potentially changing its structure and interfering with its normal activity.

For HGF, the researchers identified two especially important locations, Y198 and Y250. Both lie within the region involved in attaching to the c-met receptor.

When these sites undergo nitration, HGF becomes less capable of connecting with its receptor. The result is similar to a key that has become damaged and can no longer operate its intended lock.

This disruption could have important consequences for aging muscles. Even if the body continues producing HGF, chemical changes may prevent the protein from properly activating the stem cells needed for tissue repair. The researchers believe this mechanism may contribute to age-related muscle wasting and declining regenerative capacity.

"HGF is not necessarily missing as we age," explains Tatsumi. "Rather, it can be chemically altered after it is made. That led us to wonder whether a compound with strong antioxidant capacity might protect HGF, either by preventing nitration or by compensating for the functional loss it causes."

Scientists Test Two Powerful Sulfur Compounds

To investigate that possibility, the team studied two compounds with strong antioxidant properties: glutathione trisulfide (GSSSG) and lipoic acid trisulfide (LASSS).

Antioxidants can help limit certain types of chemical damage caused by reactive molecules. Such damage can interfere with proteins and other essential components of cells, particularly when the body's normal protective systems become less effective.

The two compounds belong to a chemical family called trisulfides. Their defining feature is a chain of three sulfur atoms connected to one another. This arrangement gives them unusual chemical properties, including an ability to participate in reactions involving the transfer of electrons, known as redox reactions.

Because these reactions play important roles in cellular chemistry, trisulfides have attracted growing interest as potential ingredients in new medicines.

In the first set of experiments, both compounds reduced nitration at the two vulnerable sites on HGF. However, preventing this chemical modification did not completely restore the protein's ability to attach to c-met.

The scientists therefore increased the amount of trisulfide used relative to HGF. They changed the molar ratio, which compares the number of molecules of each substance, from 1:4000 to 1:8000.

That adjustment produced an unexpected result.

An Unexpected Discovery Creates "Super HGF"

At the higher concentration, LASSS did much more than protect HGF from chemical damage. It also dramatically improved the protein's ability to bind to its receptor.

Compared with untreated HGF, the protein exposed to LASSS showed more than twice the binding affinity for c-met. In other words, it could attach to its target receptor much more strongly, potentially enhancing a critical step in the muscle repair process.

The treatment also made HGF more resistant to the loss of function caused by nitration, particularly at the Y198 site.

Notably, the effect was specific to LASSS. Although GSSSG had also reduced nitration in the earlier experiments, it did not produce the same improvement in receptor binding.

"This exceeded our expectations," comments Tatsumi. "We knew trisulfides had diverse biological functions, but we never expected that simply mixing HGF with LASSS would produce such a striking effect.

"What this tells us is that LASSS does more than simply neutralize reactive molecules. It may interact directly with HGF and induce a subtle structural change, creating an enhanced 'Super HGF' form that binds c-met more strongly and resists nitration."

The researchers suspect that LASSS interacts with HGF in a way that slightly alters the protein's three-dimensional shape. Because a protein's shape helps determine how well it interacts with other molecules, even a small structural adjustment could substantially change its activity.

The result is what the team describes as "Super HGF," a potentially enhanced form of the body's existing muscle repair signal.

Importantly, stronger receptor binding does not automatically establish that muscle regeneration itself has improved. Additional experiments will be needed to determine whether this molecular enhancement translates into better muscle healing and strength.

Mouse Experiments Reveal Promising Protection

After observing the effects in laboratory experiments, the researchers wanted to determine whether LASSS could also protect HGF inside living muscle tissue.

They used mice subjected to tail suspension, an established experimental method for studying muscle atrophy. By reducing normal weight bearing and muscle use, this technique produces some of the changes associated with prolonged inactivity, including muscle deterioration.

Mice that received LASSS before the experiment showed significantly less HGF nitration than untreated animals. This suggested that the compound's ability to protect the muscle repair protein was not limited to controlled laboratory conditions.

Once again, GSSSG failed to produce the same protective result.

These findings provide early evidence that LASSS can influence the chemical processes affecting HGF within living animals. However, the mouse experiments demonstrated protection against nitration, not that LASSS restored lost muscle mass or improved physical strength.

The researchers emphasize that studies involving aging animals are still necessary to establish the compound's effectiveness and safety in vivo, meaning within a living organism.

A Potential New Strategy Against Age-Related Muscle Loss

The discovery could eventually contribute to treatments aimed at maintaining muscle function during aging or extended periods of inactivity.

Muscle deterioration is not limited to older adults. It can also occur during prolonged bed rest or other situations in which muscles are used less frequently. When muscle repair mechanisms become impaired, recovering lost strength and function can become especially challenging.

Rather than replacing the body's natural repair machinery, the approach explored in this study seeks to protect and enhance an existing biological signal. If the benefits can be confirmed in future studies, strengthening HGF activity could become one strategy for supporting muscle regeneration.

The scientists also believe that the underlying effects of LASSS on HGF may extend across species. That raises the possibility of applications not only in human medicine but also in veterinary care, particularly for aging companion animals such as dogs and cats.

For now, the findings represent an early step toward understanding how a naturally occurring muscle repair pathway might be strengthened. Whether LASSS can safely and effectively preserve muscle function during aging remains an open question.

Still, the unexpected discovery that a sulfur-based compound can both protect and enhance a critical repair protein offers a promising direction for future research, with the long-term goal of helping people maintain mobility, independence, and a better quality of life as they grow older.

Materials provided by Kyushu University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4320. Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

There's a new Arc Raiders patch that's fairly small, but one with fixes everyone is going to appreciate.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4319. KRÜ Blaze recover from opening map loss to beat Shopify Rebellion Gold and reach final

KRÜ Blaze dropped the first map and then took the next three on Saturday 31 October. The win reverses their upper bracket semi-final defeat to Shopify Rebellion Gold and sends the Argentine-based side into the final of the VCT Game Changers Championship 2026. Shopify Rebellion Gold’s campaign ends with the loss.

The result also cuts against the power rankings. Shopify Rebellion Gold arrived as the 10th-ranked team with a rating of 1782. KRÜ Blaze sit 20th on 1742, although their 63-21 record across 84 rated matches is the stronger of the two.

Shopify Rebellion Gold struck first, taking a 47-minute opening map. KRÜ Blaze levelled on the quickest map of the series, which lasted 37 minutes, and edged ahead with a 50-minute third.

The fourth map was by some distance the longest of the night at 70 minutes. KRÜ Blaze closed it out to settle the best-of-five without needing a decider.

The meeting on 27 October had been far more one-sided. Shopify Rebellion Gold won that upper bracket semi-final 2-0, which pushed KRÜ Blaze into the lower half of the draw. Before that, KRÜ Blaze had opened their playoff run by beating Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper bracket quarter-finals.

Saturday’s victory was KRÜ Blaze’s third successive series win in the lower bracket. Both earlier wins were sweeps. They beat Team Liquid Brazil 2-0 in the quarter-finals, then dispatched MIBR GC by the same score in the semi-finals.

That run means they have won seven of the eight maps played since dropping out of the upper bracket. They also came into the event as winners of the Latin America regional final, where they beat Akave Esports Black 3-1.

#4318. 10 Action-Adventure Games That Are Unexpected Masterpieces

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

The action-adventure genre is one of the broadest in the entire video game industry, encompassing countless experiences ranging from stealth and hack-and-slash to horror and beat 'em ups.

Thanks to this broad definition, countless masterpieces fall under its umbrella, including many that, unfortunately, haven't achieved the popularity they deserve due to fierce competition.

Even within the realm of major blockbusters, not all underrated titles are obscure indie games—there are games that have fallen just short of mainstream success, though I'm here to help rectify that.

So, in order to shed light on some lesser-known campaigns that haven't yet cemented their undeniable excellence in the collective consciousness, I invite you to explore this list of ten action-adventure games that are unexpected masterpieces.

As the least recognized work from Tango Gameworks, a studio that has certainly gifted us with numerous magnificent journeys, Ghostwire: Tokyo stands out among the games with the greatest disparity between its quality and its fame.

Boasting one of the finest atmospheres crafted this decade, wandering the streets of Shibuya, soaring across rooftops, and taking down the most terrifying yokai imaginable is, by far, one of my highlights of the decade.

Whether in stealth or direct magical combat, tackling one of its turbulent side quests or hunting for collectibles, the game strikes an outstanding balance between making each mechanic satisfying while still maintaining a constant sense of terror in its setting.

As far as first-person games go, Ghostwire: Tokyo is part of the most immersive, rewarding, and distinctive I've played this generation, which is saying something considering the titans with which it shares category.

As the years have gone by, games that adhere to the Metroidvania philosophy have become one of my greatest obsessions, which inevitably led me to fall in love with Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo.

Its ability to capture the nostalgia of the Game Boy Advance era while boasting the refined design and execution of modern products demonstrates its creators' immeasurable talent, who also imbued it with an impressive thematic personality.

The critiques of various strategic production industries resonate with our current times, while in the process, the game leverages the yoyo as a central gameplay element to make traversal, combat, exploration, and customization an absolute delight that's also pretty unique.

Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo is among the finest indie titles I've enjoyed in the last couple of years, and anything other than recognizing it as brilliant is to underestimate its potential.

If you're interested in unfairly criticized titles, I recommend checking out these ten underrated action-adventure games that were badly reviewed.

As someone who didn't experience the franchise's heyday, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance not only caught me completely off guard, but I can think of very few resurrections that have felt so powerful.

The absolute masterwork of action and platforming that this title is results in frankly mind-blowing sequences, flowing seamlessly between both dimensions to deliver a thrilling adventure that doesn't let you breathe for a second.

As you unlock combos, powers, and movement abilities, you encounter an ever-increasing series of challenges that push the game's mechanics to their limits, which are meticulously refined to ensure you have complete control over every pixel.

Few titles in 2025 felt as satisfying to complete 100%, so Shinobi: Art of Vengeance stands as a masterfully unexpected example that, when you don't know what to do with your old IPs, outsourcing to an indie studio to work on them is the best possible idea.

The Legend of Zelda's heirs number in the hundreds of thousands, but that didn't stop Death's Door from emerging as one of its most intelligent and charismatic great-great-grandchildren.

The game perfectly understands the enjoyment that lies in discovery and exploration through iteration, inviting us on a diverse adventure with plenty of colorful biomes, enemies, characters, and circumstances that evoke all kinds of emotions.

Curiosity, fear, happiness, sadness, worry... The title silently manages a multitude of emotions both thematically and in its gameplay, limiting progression to allow for exploration of its expansive world at a prodigious pace.

When discussing isometric titles that combine action, platforming, and puzzles in the best possible way, Death's Door is at the description's forefront, though it's the ease and finesse with which it achieves this that's truly unexpected.

Castlevania is a series that went through some difficult years after the turn of the century, and it wasn't until Castlevania: Lords of Shadow arrived that the IP unexpectedly found some relief amidst so many setbacks, astonishingly becoming the best-selling game in the entire IP.

MercurySteam crafted one of the most beautiful and satisfying hack-and-slash games in the genre's history, finally adapting the saga's formula perfectly to 3D without losing an ounce of its core identity.

The whip feels better than ever, as do the movement mechanics, the puzzles, and the progression systems, all enhanced in the best possible way thanks to a magnificently crafted story and characters that keep you on the edge of your seat until the very last second.

Castlevania: Lords of Shadow completely forgoes being conceptually innovative, but the sacrifice, given it guaranteed us an extremely excellent title in all its facets, was totally worth it even when nobody was betting on such a resounding success.

If you enjoy discovering incredible titles without proper recognition, I recommend these ten best action-adventure games forgotten by time.

In the years when God of War slowed down, and Devil May Cry practically disappeared, a third icon emerged from absolutely nowhere to keep the hack-and-slash genre alive (with Bayonetta's permission): Darksiders.

Drawing inspiration from both Santa Monica Studio's work and The Legend of Zelda, Vigil Games crafted a splendidly elaborate tale and setting within Judeo-Christian mythology, one of the least explored in the video game industry.

Giant bosses based on satisfying gimmicks, varied and refreshing puzzles that make the most of War's arsenal and movement capabilities, phenomenal art design for both environments and enemies... It's the complete package.

That the company's first title would be such a presentation of knowledge in the genre's fundamentals was unforeseen even for the team itself, but much more for the hundreds of thousands who, like me, stumbled upon Darksiders by chance and have been hooked ever since.

Returning to the topic of franchises forced to reinvent themselves to adapt to modern times, not even the most optimistic projections for the Tomb Raider reboot could have predicted the absolute brilliance it would become.

Going back to Lara Croft's origins resulted in one of the quintessential action-adventure games of the entire generation, achieving an astonishing symphony of survival mechanics, realistic yet compelling gunplay, and simply fantastic settings and stories.

Each set piece surpasses the last, and the spectacular scenery contrasts perfectly with the brutal and tense story the legendary archaeologist faces, all while possessing the intriguing premise of not yet being the intrepid adventurer we all know, but rather a young, still-innocent graduate.

From concept to execution, Tomb Raider is a tapestry of sound decisions that, among other things, reminded Uncharted fans that Nathan Drake only managed to run because Lara Croft walked first.

I know that nowadays we're used to indie masterpieces being released every couple of months, but back in the day, before that was the norm, Hyper Light Drifter arrived like a hurricane of grandeur.

Taking Dark Souls' harshness, non-linearity, and disorientation, Heart Machine assembled an adventure that is both cryptic and captivating, where the gameplay and narrative direction are entirely in the player's hands.

Where to go and why are questions that only the user can answer through exploration, embarking on an intense and introspective journey where bosses and secrets abound, motivating us to explore every last corner of its silent world.

Along with gorgeous pixel art, a remarkable sound design, and a simple yet perfect gameplay loop, Hyper Light Drifter built a castle with just a few blocks, a feat reserved only for the greatest.

If you're looking for modern games to get lost in, I recommend the ten best adventure games of the 2020s (so far).

The reviews for Asura's Wrath were so scathing that it took me a decade to finally deign to play it, and the sheer shock of finishing it in tears when the credits rolled was beyond words.

Yes, every single one of the comments regarding its poor gameplay was, is, and will be correct, since it's a beat 'em up where the best parts of the gameplay are the on-rails shooting and quick-time events, and that doesn't exactly reflect well on a title of this genre.

Regardless, when you have such an incredible plot, abundant with charismatic characters, memorable scenes, robust mythology, and eccentrically immeasurable cinematics, I couldn't care less that every encounter boils down to mashing the attack button a hundred times a second.

The intercosmic scale that Asura's Wrath handles in its presentation and spectacle is monumental, unique, and emotional enough to overlook its mediocre mechanics, being the only case in the entire genre where it's a masterpiece even without being fun in the traditional sense.

Bucking the trend in the genre, whose disdain for stealth became evident in the last decade, Arkane Studios made a tremendous statement in 2012 with Dishonored's release.

Coming from another underrated gem, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, the studio embraced the lingering force of immersive sims and materialized it into a project that excels as both a stealth game and an action-adventure game.

Boasting some of the best level design in video game history, along with a story that evolves based on the player's actions rather than dialogue choices, Dishonored is one of the century's defining power fantasies.

Between Dunwall's perfect setting, the outstanding array of gadgets and powers that allow for creative and expansive use of stealth and violence, and the majestic musical pieces that accompany us, it's clear that the love for stealth games will never die as long as this IP remains available.

Years go by, and I still wonder if the genre has enough strength to produce a title that surpasses Dishonored, but for now, it remains on the throne without any concern about being replaced.

In this list, we'll discuss our picks for the best action-adventure games that go beyond a hundred hours, from RPGs to known open-world titles.

#4317. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Update 1.1 Adds Quality Of Life Improvements, Boosts Performance, and Adds Pettable Animals

We've been enjoying The Blood of Dawnwalker, one of the year's biggest games, but its release was a little rough around the edges. It took a lot of feedback from fans for developer Rebel Wolves to prioritize higher framerates at launch for consoles, but even then, the game certainly struggled at times on my PlayStation 5. Today, the game's first major update drops, and it aims to smooth some of those performance issues and introduce a few quality-of-life features.

The trailer above highlights combat-specific improvements, like improved targeting and animations, and a less restrictive camera. Rebel Wolves is also lowering the health of wolves and boars, who previously remained tanky even into the later hours of the game, and it should be easier to disengage from combat, should you choose to do so. For casual players, there's a new difficulty mode; what was previously "Story" mode has been renamed "Forgiving," while the new version of "Story" mode adds additional combat assists.

Rebel Wolves has also added some new features outside of combat. A new Daught of Mind Rebirth potion allows you to respec your skill tree, re-allocating time and skill points spent to switch up your build. You can also increase the size of subtitles (an option I'm always grateful for) and pet dogs and cats. Finally, the Shadowstep and Planeshift systems should be more responsive now – here's hoping I have an easier time teleporting onto rooftops instead of the wall right below them.

Those are the major, most visible highlights, but players can view the full patch notes here to see the hundreds of other minor improvements that aim to squash bugs, reduce crashes, and improve stability.

For more on The Blood of Dawnwalker, you can check out our review, in which our reviewer admires the swings the developers took, even though they don't always pay off. You can also check out our coverage hub for our issue devoted to The Blood of Dawnwalker, including interviews with its ex-Witcher development team.

#4315. Dispatch's Anniversary Update Brings Commentary Track, Storyboard Mode, And Mobile Port

Dispatch, a superhero-themed workplace comedy from last year, celebrates its one-year anniversary today. While it was released episodically, the first batch dropped on October 22. It was received well, with strong performances from a star-studded cast (including Breaking Bad star Aaron Paul) and filled a niche left vacant by Telltale Games' absence from the gaming world in recent years. Today, developer AdHoc announced a batch of anniversary content, and some of it drops today.

First, there's a new way to play Dispatch: storyboard mode. This option lets you play through the whole experience using the original animatics – rough placeholder sketches that the artists used to sync images up to the voice-over. It's a fun behind-the-scenes look at the game's development that we don't get very often. In that same vein, the cast and crew recorded DVD-style commentary tracks to play over the game, making jokes and sharing insight into the development process. A press release says there are over 16 hours of commentary from the game's development team (like art director Derek Stratton and creative directors Dennis Lenart and Nick Herman) as well as some of the cast, including Aaron Paul, Laura Bailey, and Erin Yvette.

Storyboard and Commentary modes are included in the game's deluxe edition, which you can upgrade to for $10.99. Both modes are available today.

If you haven't played the game yet, AdHoc has announced a new way to do so; Dispatch is coming to mobile platforms on December 9. It's been rebuilt to support touch controls and vertical play, and it will be available on iOS and Android. You can even play the first half of the game for free – the first four episodes are included, but you'll need to pay $19.99 to play the rest.

Finally, AdHoc announced new merch, including a book created alongside publisher Lost in Cult called Dispatch: Design Works, which is both an art book and a "making-of" book. There's also a live game soundtrack concert in Los Angeles featuring Thot Squad, Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury, Fartbarf, and Dispatch composer Andrew Arcadi with the SDN Company Band. It will be held at Avalon Hollywood on December 3, but it won't be livestreamed, so you'll need to grab a ticket to see the event. The press release states that people who signed up for updates from adhocstudio.com will be the first in line to purchase tickets.

#4312. Tenebris Somnia Review – A Hair-Raising And Entertaining Throwback

Tenebris Somnia channels the old-school appeal of classic point-and-click adventures, survival horror, and full-motion-video (FMV) experiences, then smartly modernizes them to create a creepy, entertaining experience. Surviving the twisted threats of a demonic dream world is a tightly packed adventure that rewards you with what’s essentially an impressive indie horror film peppered throughout. It’s a nightmare you may not want to wake up from.

The blend of live-action and in-game storytelling works well in Tenebris Somina’s adventure, which begins when protagonist Julia visits the apartment of her filmmaker ex-boyfriend, Ivan, after suffering recurring nightmares of him being massacred by monsters. What begins as a well-meaning check-in on his status spirals down an unsettling rabbit hole when Julia’s worst fears are realized and then some. The dialogue-free tale presents a scary but fascinating exploration of obsession, both in art and in romance, that constantly delivers surprising, and at times upsetting, revelations during its eight-hour runtime. While Tenebris Somnia sometimes leans a little too far into “tell, don’t show” territory when explaining the cool lore of its supernatural threats, I never felt lost or confused about the wild things that regularly unfold on screen.

FMV experiences are nothing new, but Tenebris Somnia’s live-action scenes are a highlight. They’re well shot, sport impressively gruesome practical effects, and even present visual clues that make them important to gameplay. These scenes are additive, never taking too much time away from the in-game action, and they feel well placed to elicit the strongest emotional response. I also appreciate how the live scenes fit thematically, as much of Tenebris Somnia’s tale centers on a horror film shot by Ivan and Julia that significantly impacted their former relationship; at times, it’s like watching a movie about the movie. While I enjoy smaller moments, like opening a door to trigger a live-action jump scare, the filmmaking succeeds in selling Julia's emotions and the cast's reactions. Seeing real fear, concern, and determination in Julia’s eyes as she navigates a dreamworld made up of Ivan’s memories helped endear me to what would otherwise be a featureless pixel sprite.

Gameplay may look unimpressive due to its old-school adventure game presentation, but Tenebris Somnia’s spin on familiar survival-horror mechanics hits the right notes. Taking place entirely within a dreamlike version of a four-story apartment building, you’ll traverse floors collecting and combining objects and deciphering clues to solve well-crafted puzzles. I’m impressed by how well the game’s puzzles make the most of its limited graphical presentation, including clever scenarios involving mirror/screen reflections I won’t spoil, and how consistently creative they are. One devious exercise even utilizes the game’s limited save points as an unexpected resource in a way that changes how you approach your adventure going forward. No matter how strange puzzles become, they are never opaque, requiring just enough out-of-the-box thinking to make me feel smart when I connect the dots.

Battling grotesque monsters (which, naturally, look even creepier in live-action) also feels good, with melee and gunplay sporting deliberate animations reminiscent of classic adventure games without feeling mechanically clunky. Taking on multiple enemies by swinging a pipe or blowing them away with a shotgun feels better than it looks, and the most intense encounters end just as they approach the line of becoming overwhelming.

Boss battles, perhaps most unexpectedly for a largely puzzle-focused adventure, are fun and distinct from each other, be it wave-based bouts against small gremlin-like foes, protecting a fragile effigy of yourself from a parade of demented house servants, or battling literal mirror images of a tentacled flesh monster the Resident Evil series would be proud to claim. Managing limited ammo and health strikes a good balance of feeling tense but not oppressive. Playing conservatively is rewarding, as few non-boss threats need to be engaged if you can evade them well enough. But when I did find myself down to my last bullet or on the verge of death, Tenebris Somnia lets you feel the pinch just long enough before dropping a box of bullets or a health vial at the right moment.

Tenebris Somnia mines the enjoyable nostalgia of playing the horror games of yesteryear without feeling dated in the worst way. Weaving a solid indie horror film adds to the experience rather than feeling like a gimmick. The result is a captivating, well-executed survival-horror romp that maintains a hair-raising atmosphere with a fraction of the pixels of other genre giants.

#4311. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4310. DC Dark Legion tier list - With Supergirl Woman of Tomorrow

I ranked every single hero and villain from the best to the likes of Bazooka Bro and company in the DC Dark Legion tier list.

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 2.2.28 - Added: Superman Death Metal I don't often find games that combine a lot of elements beautifully without leaning too much in one direction (like an overly gacha-fied one). Dark Legion does it wonderfully, and the result is an amazing experience you can enjoy playing both casually and more intensely.

To give you a hand and make things a lot simpler, I've ranked every villain and superhero in this DC Dark Legion tier list, pitting them against one another.

As you might expect, Superman (Clark Kent) is indeed top-tier. But how well do the rest of the heroes rank? That's what we're about to take a look at. Gacha-wise, you will have a blast As a true gacha lover, I can honestly say there aren't a lot of F2P-friendly mobile offerings out there. For this one, though, you can make all the Legendary heroes work, and for the most part, you won't even feel the need to spend money. Of course, you might be tempted to do so when you see the starter bundle, but I'll cover that in more detail in another article.  Oh, and before you go ahead and summon, make sure you also claim the latest DC Dark Legion codes! The best superheroes and villains to invest in If you want to have a shortlist of the strongest superheroes to invest in, I'd say go for the following:

From the very beginning, you'll start with Green Arrow, Mera and Wonder Woman - these three are extremely F2P-friendly, and they will help carry you throughout. Of course, if you get Superman, that's a no-brainer. Invest in him ASAP. As for Harley Quinn, you will get her for free from the sign-in event. She's also pretty awesome!

Now, let's dive into the DC Dark Legion tier list! S+ tier  |  S tier  |  A tier  |  B tier  |  C tier

Superman is currently the crème de la crème , which earns him the spot at the peak of our Dark Legion tier list. He is a melee fighter who is tanky, deals insane amounts of damage, and can also freeze enemies. He has it all, and if you deploy allies from the Superman Family, he will also gain additional ATK.

The Joker is a great disabler - he can be a good addition to most teams out there, and so can Green Lantern, but for a different reason (he's a supporter). Finally, Sinestro has outstanding DPS, so if you feel like you lack damage, try to get him.

It's also worth mentioning that not all of these characters go together that well. Ideally, you will want to deploy the ones that can buff each other passively, so try mixing and matching them with some of the A-tier options.

Wonder Woman is a mere Legendary hero (just like Green Arrow and Mera), but she is so incredibly good and easy to upgrade that she's easily S-tier. With her Ultimate, she can deal damage to enemies in a cone and stun them, while her skills make her incredibly tanky. Oh, and she can also shield an ally!

Green Arrow is a classic ranged DPS. He deals both AoE and single-target damage, and can be easily upgraded since he's one of the first heroes you get.

Mera is a healer that outperforms any other, which puts her at the top of this DC Dark Legion tier list. She can AoE heal the entire team with her ultimate, while with Healing Waters, she can also apply healing over time.

Batman is a great hero to get - he is a lesser version of Superman in a way (their skills obviously differ, but their positions are similar). He can be obtained for about $2 from the starter pack, and if you want to start off on the right foot by spending a couple of bucks, he is a safe choice.

Doctor Fate is an amazing guardian. He can even be a higher tier if you happen to get a lot of his shards and max him out. He can protect allies and tank quite a bit, and let's be honest, his design is so good!

Oh, and have a look at our guide on the DC Dark Legion best teams too, won't you?

In the B tier, we have some viable heroes that can replace the higher-tier options. The Flash, for instance, is a decent supporter, but he's not the best. Not even close. In all honesty, he doesn't even come close to Mera.

Red Hood is a decent hero for DPS if you get him early on. I personally like him and use him until I manage to get someone better. Robin is an assassin, but when faced with so many enemies, he tends to fall off, especially in the late game.

All of the heroes that are struggling at the bottom of this DC Dark Legion tier list are subpar. The Epic ones are a given (you'll only use them to complete your collection), but the Legendary or Mythic heroes ranked here don't really bring much to the team. I recommend you avoid using them if possible. Okay, you can use them in the early game, but look for alternatives almost immediately.

#4309. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4308. A Mass Effect 5 Trailer Featuring Liara Appears To Have Leaked Following BioWare's Closure

In case you missed the tragic news yesterday, EA laid off 400 employees this week, including all of BioWare. The studio behind Mass Effect, Dragon Age, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and more, has been shut down, and its last remaining project was canceled. The game in question was a fifth entry in the Mass Effect universe, and BioWare shared very little about it – not even an official name. Following the studio's closure, however, a trailer for the sci-fi sequel started circulating around the internet.

While no official BioWare representatives have confirmed that the footage is real, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier claims that it is. Schreier has a history of credible reporting in the field, and was the first to break the news about the layoffs. IGN has also stated that it confirmed the trailer's legitimacy.

If you want to see for yourself, you can watch the trailer on Reddit.

"The following is in-engine footage form our small team," text at the start of the video reads. "It uses our pre-production assets." The footage shows no gameplay, but includes a good-looking CG cutscene of a new protagonist speaking with an asari woman in a crowded bar. As he tells her about his life, we see glimpses of him as a soldier, then as some kind of spy, traveling to several planets to track down conflicts and "stopping them before they start." After the asari woman reveals that she's been "starting the fires" he's trying to prevent, another woman behind her lowers a hood. This new woman reveals herself as Liara T'Soni, one of Mass Effect's most iconic characters.

Then, Liara and the protagonist team up to take out the woman at the bar and her henchmen, using guns and telekinetic abilities. The trailer fades to black, then fades back in to reveal the game's would-be title: Mass Effect Universe. It's a great-looking trailer – it's a shame the game will never see the light of day.

#4307. d4v41 and Jinggg leave Paper Rex after 7th–8th Champions finish, Pacific place secure

Paper Rex has parted with captain d4v41 and Jinggg, two Masters Toronto winners, after an early exit at Champions 2026. With its VCT Pacific partner place secure, the Singapore organisation is rebuilding by choice as free agency opens to every region.

Paper Rex has broken up the core of its VALORANT roster. The Singapore organisation is parting with its captain and one of its best-known players as the 2027 season approaches. d4v41 had been with Paper Rex since its founding in 2020. He played first on its CS:GO roster, then moved with the team to VALORANT. Jinggg joined on 28 September 2021.

Neither player has named a destination. In the farewell video Paper Rex released, d4v41 said he was moving to a new team. Jinggg wrote on X that he was excited about what comes next. d4v41 also asked fans to keep supporting the organisation after both have gone.

The split follows a season that faded at the end. Paper Rex were runners-up at both Masters Santiago and Masters London earlier in 2026. At Champions in Shanghai, they lost 2-0 to LOUD in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 7 October. A 2-1 defeat to T1 in lower-bracket round one ended their run on 9 October. The event carried a $2,250,000 prize pool. LOUD went on to beat Team Vitality in the final.

The pair leave with a long record together. Jinggg helped Paper Rex to second place at Masters Copenhagen 2022. He was also part of the run to the Champions 2023 final, where the team were runners-up. Liquipedia lists both players in the line-up that won VCT 2025 Masters Toronto.

The changes are not forced by the league. The organisation is owned by IMPLS Entertainment Pte Ltd. Riot has cut the number of partner teams in each region from ten to eight for 2027–28. That leaves 32 across the four regions.

The Pacific format rewards that security. The eight partners receive seeded places at Kickoff in January 2027. Four further places go to teams that come through open qualifiers. Paper Rex can therefore reshape its roster without needing to qualify.

Two Masters winners on the open market could matter well beyond the Pacific. EMEA’s eight partners for 2027 are Fnatic, BBL Esports, FUT Esports, Team Heretics, Team Liquid, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp and Team Vitality. Under Riot’s open qualifier rules, most regions require three of a team’s five players to come from that region. Teams must also keep three of five players between events to carry their progress forward. Those limits will frame how far any club can rebuild around new signings.

Khalish has been part of Paper Rex since our founding in 2020, starting first on our CS:GO Roster and transitioning with the team to VALORANT. We'll always remember the laughs, the op shots, and every achievement through the years.

From everyone at Paper Rex, we wish @d4v41vlr… pic.twitter.com/UgWKD4QfOj

Later in November, open qualifiers get under way. The season’s first Masters event follows in February 2027.

#4306. Dragon Ball Z Dokkan Battle tier list

LR and TUR characters are the cream of the crop at the moment, and we have ranked them according to their power on this Dokkan Battle tier list.

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version - 6.6.5

Let's be honest, power creep in this game is real. If you're unfamiliar, that means the new units are usually just better than the old ones. As a result, the meta is ever-changing, and keeping up with it can be challenging if you are a returning player.

If you are a veteran player, of course, you have your own Dokkan Battle tier list in mind and nothing is going to change that, but hopefully, this article can help new players (and returning players) get some perspective on the current state of the meta.

I say the current state of the meta because you never know when Bandai Namco will decide to release a new Extreme-Z Awakening (EZA) or something that will change everything completely. Remember when Goku was considered to be the best unit in the game? Yeah, it's been a while, hasn't it?

Of course, ranking every unit in Dokkan would make no sense for various reasons, but most importantly, you just want to know which units are the best in the game, right? So, we've decided to rank the top 10 best LR units in Dokkan Battle and also the 10 best TUR.

For any new players who are wondering what exactly TUR means, let's clear things up. TUR stands for transcended ultra rare, which means the unit has been Dokkan awakened from a level 100 UR and can go higher than level 120 and SA higher than 10.

With that out of the way, let's get into our Dokkan Battle tier list.

No surprises here as Incomparable Radiance Super Saiyan Goku + Super Saiyan Vegeta (Angel) is the best LR unit in the game. What is there to say about this one, really? It has everything. Damage, defense, broad category synergies, and, of course, the Super Vegito mechanics, on top of massive ATK/DEF stats. It's a must-have for anniversary events (and beyond).

This version of Goku (Ultimate Saiyan Power Roar Super Saiyan 3 Goku (GT) (Golden Giant Ape)), transforms into a Golden Giant Ape under specific conditions, such as when his HP falls to 70% or less or starting from the fifth turn of battle. His abilities include a significant boost to Ki and Attack/Defense stats, with a high chance of performing critical hits. He also receives additional Ki when obtaining AGL Ki Spheres, enhancing his combat effectiveness. His Super Attack, Ki Blast Super Kamehameha, deals supreme damage to enemies while raising his Attack for three turns.

"All-Out Super Attack" Super Saiyan Gohan (Teen) is the "Kamehameha" category leader. He grants Ki +3 and a massive +200% boost to HP, ATK, and DEF, embodying Teen Gohan's iconic Kamehameha clash with Cell from the Cell Saga.

His kit features powerful Super Attacks with stun potential, a passive that ramps up ATK and DEF with Hybrid Saiyans and Movie Heroes allies. and HP recovery below 50%, peaking in long fights like Red Zone with millions in damage output.

That said, his slow startup and early-game fragility (DEF around 200k pre-Super) make him less ideal for short battles, requiring specific team synergies to get by. It is best to pair him with Hybrid Saiyans or Kamehameha units like LR STR SSJ2 Gohan

His kit delivers ATK & DEF (+260%, +100% on attack), Ki and HP boosts from spheres, and a game-changing Active Skill against Goku’s Family, that can dish out at 10-15M damage and 500k+ DEF in events like Red Zone.

His early DEF (200k pre-Super) and tricky Ki links (e.g., Fierce Battle) are problematic, and it demands specific team-building for Broly to work.

Gamma 1 feels like a gatekeeper to the top five TUR in Dokkan Battle. He's just great all around, a very solid unit that should not be underestimated.

If this Kale variant had a bit of help from other units, she would be ranked even higher. I'm a bit biased since this is my favourite unit for quite some time now, but once she transforms, she can just take over any battle. With that said, she does need some help to get there.

There's not a lot to say about our top 3 units on this part of a tier list.

We start our top 10 with Super 17. We could argue this card's placement on the list, but no matter how we slice it, it couldn't be much higher. Remember, these are the best TUR in the game, so we have to judge them accordingly.

This is the end of our Dokkan Battle tier list. If you have any suggestions, leave a comment below.

#4305. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Review - Silver Bullet

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 arrives at a crossroads for the series, thanks in large part to the inconsistent quality of recent entries. With a shaky predecessor, Infinity Ward had a lot to repair and conclude, especially with 4 set to bookend the rebooted Modern Warfare series. Fortunately, backed up by a fun campaign, thrilling multiplayer, and loads of new modes and content, Modern Warfare 4 makes up for the past and then some.

Modern Warfare 4 continues after the events of 2023’s Modern Warfare 3, with Captain Price hellbent on stopping Makarov and his higher-ups. The story features shifting perspectives, from a new group of ragtag Korean soldiers to familiar characters like Gaz. The character dynamics harken back to the original trilogy, especially in the boots-on-the-ground missions with the South Korean unit, led by Park (played by Beef actor Young Mazino).

For a series that, at least recently, has been more spectacle than story, giving the stakes the time they deserve is nice. While it moves away from the stealthy and modernized elements, it makes sense for the matters at hand. The majority of Modern Warfare 4’s attempts at wrapping up the overarching plot of the rebooted series works, but it rushes through some character arcs and story beats in uneven fashion. Furthermore, much of the game’s cast, especially Mads Mikkelson’s Archer and Prisca Kim’s Ri Ju-Young, are underutilized, which is a shame since they both deliver great performances.

Despite the shortcomings of the campaign, Call of Duty's bread and butter, multiplayer, still delivers. While it doesn’t have the fluidity of Black Ops’ newer entries, the customization and design of weapons and maps make it worth digging into. From small, intimate shooting galleries with Mumbai and Nautical to wide free-for-alls like Coal and Reactor U92, the range helps maintain excitement, even if it gets repetitive over time.

The variety of multiplayer modes keeps things fresh on the battlefield. Returning modes like standard Team Deathmatch and Kill Confirmed continue that enjoyable competitive flair that made them the stars that they are. However, new modes like Combat Outpost and Hijack fit right into the already great lineup. In particular, Combat Outpost upscales your typical 6v6 player count to 24v24, leading to more action and teamwork. Hanging onto a team’s tank, shooting enemies from afar, and taking back outposts is exhilarating, even if it can all go bad moments later by a well-placed RPG shot.

Even after hours of gameplay, the variety of options to craft your perfect gun is impressive. Figuring out the best scope, ammo, stock, and muzzle, as well as the advantages and disadvantages of them, is a fun way of customizing your playstyle. Gunny, a mechanic that helps optimize your gun for certain styles, can help with decision paralysis, but I rarely used it. Not many FPSs go that far and Modern Warfare 4’s commitment to the feature makes it stand out.

The newest mode, DMZ, impresses out of the gate. After a few flat attempts in the past, this is the definitive Call of Duty extraction shooter, whether you play solo, or in duos or trios. Immediately, you’re thrust into the wide open world of Hajin and left to fend for yourselves with what you have and what you can gather and extract. Fans of Arc Raiders and Marathon should feel right at home as the gameplay borrows from the typical extraction shooter experience. Intense, action-packed moments keep you coming back after every win or loss. And the excellent gunplay and level design elevate it into something worthwhile, no matter how you play.

Despite not encountering many live players during my time in Hajin in DMZ, it still proves challenging, even for seasoned pros. The world is not your friend, and taking risks can come at a high cost. A good team, as well as a thoughtful loadout and traits, are required to survive. The unpredictability of it all keeps you on your toes, making for an exciting addition to the already strong multiplayer suite.

Regardless of the mode, Modern Warfare 4 is one of the best-looking Call of Duty titles to date. New York and Paris are lifelike, and it truly embodies the realistic, modern aesthetic the series has always aimed to achieve. However, I encountered a few technical hiccups, especially in the campaign. Slow framerate plagues some high-octane scenes and texture loading is frequent across the board. These distractions are far from game-breaking, but enough to be noticeable.

While the plot execution is a bit shaky, engaging multiplayer options, including DMZ, aptly demonstrate that Infinity Ward can still deliver compelling military-FPS experiences. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is a strong return to form that serves as a solid sendoff for the rebooted subseries.

#4304. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

#4303. Roblox Demonfall Breathing tier list

Breathing techniques are one of the most crucial features, and we have ranked all of them in this Demonfall Breathing tier list based on their value and general strengths.

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Update 5.6

Demonfall is an RPG developed by Fireheart Studio based on the Demon Slayer anime and manga. In it, you will enter the world of Demon Slayer, in which demons hunt people and demon slayers try to destroy demons. It's the circle of life... sort of.

The developers have tried to make it exciting and varied by including the ability to learn many different skills and attacks. Of course, it wouldn't be a Demon Slayer-based game if you couldn't use Breathing. Read on and find out about the styles in our Demonfall Breathing tier list.

If you're interested in other Roblox games, we have an AoTR tier list, A Universal Time tier list ranking the finest stands, a Fruit Battlegrounds fruits tier list and a lot of others that you can take a look at. Tier Character S Sun, Moon A Water, Sound, Mist, Stone, Love B Flame, Beast, Insect, Thunder C Wind, Serpent

In Demonfall, as in many other RPGs on Roblox, you will have to choose whether to join demons or to remain human. Like Tanjiro from the original anime, you will also be attacked by a demon, and if you can kill it, then you will become a demon slayer. If you lose, your health will fall to zero, and you will become a demon.

Both of these races have different abilities. Having defeated the demon, you will need to find Hayaka. She will ask you to study one of the Breathing Styles, which will help you go through the Final Selection Exam and become a real demon slayer.

Breathing Style is a sword technique. It allows people to equal the forces with demons. Each of these Styles has a certain concept and skills based on it. For example, Water skills control water, unsurprisingly. To study these Styles, you need to find special NPCs and fulfil quests for them. But to interact with them, you will first need to achieve a certain level or even prestige.

Since these Styles don't depend on your luck, you must choose which style to learn. Of course, if you change your mind, you can always use Breath Indict to forget one and try another. But it takes a lot of time, which is why we created a Demonfall Breathing tier list with all Styles ranked from the best to the worst.

Sun As in the original anime, Sun Breathing is incredibly powerful. It can deal great damage in close combat. Also, you can break blocks, which allows you to play aggressively. However, to study Sun Breathing, you will need to spend a lot of time to Level up and get prestige. Moon This one is the most difficult one to get. You first need to have the conditions for becoming a hybrid, and then the conditions for Moon Breathing. However, your efforts will be worth it, since this style is very powerful and has various instant attacks and combos.

Water It is one of the Breathing Styles you can study at the beginning of your adventure. The skills of this style are perfect for both punishment and aggression. With it, you can also make complex combo chains. Mist In the original anime, this Style was used by Tokito. And in Demonfall, he can teach you this style. Mist Breathing has one of the best combo abilities. You can use fast attacks and retreat quickly. Love Love has a good combo potential. Also, your Nichirin will change. Until you attack, it will look like an ordinary sword, but during attacks, it will turn into a whip-sword.

B Tier is average in strength. Techniques in this tier can be effective in certain modes or against certain enemies. However, if possible, it is better to use higher tiers.

Flame It is one of the most balanced Breathing Styles in Demonfall. You can use Flame skills for defence, offence, and even mobility. However, because of this balance, you can't make a combo. To learn it, you will need to find Rengoku, also known as Doughnut. Beast If you like wild attacks, then you'll love the Beast. Inosuke invented Beast, and he will be able to teach it to you. However, for this, you will need to get 100 Meat, Blue Horn and Green Horn, and you will need to spend a lot of time on this. Beast Breathing is worth it, though, because you can get a couple of special Nichirins with jagged blades. Thunder It is one of the fastest Styles in the game. Although most of your skills might not cause much damage, they are very fast. It allows you to carry out deadly combos using several skills with high damage.

The weakest tier is C tier. These styles are ineffective for both PVP and PVE. While you can use them, you're better off with other Breathing Styles.

Wind Wind has the greatest range in the game. Moreover, you have three skills that can break blocks. However, you will need to attack the enemy and quickly run away to survive. Serpent This Breathing has good skills that can stun opponents or break blocks. However, Serpent Breathing attacks are quite slow.

And that's all you need to know from this Demonfall Breathing tier list. There aren't too many Styles in the game, but they are all very different in gameplay and strength. It's worth giving each of them a go to see which one suits you best!

#4302. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4301. Amazon’s Mass Effect TV Series Is Reportedly Still In Production Despite BioWare Closure

EA shut down legendary RPG developer BioWare this week, canceling its in-development fifth Mass Effect game as a result. Despite the closure, Amazon Prime’s upcoming Mass Effect streaming series will proceed as planned, according to a report by IGN.

Amazon MGM Studios began developing a Mass Effect series in 2024. At the time, Mass Effect series executive producer Mike Gamble confirmed the show isn't a retelling of the video games, saying, “The show will explore a brand-new story within the universe's timeline, and will be set after the original trilogy. It won't be a retread of Commander Shepard's story – because after all... that's YOUR story, isn’t it?”

With BioWare’s closure, one would think the series would go up in smoke, but sources within Prime Video speaking to IGN confirmed that it remains in development. Furthermore, all of the creatives involved remain so. This includes showrunners Doug Jung (The Cloverfield Paradox, Star Trek Beyond) and Daniel Casey (F9: The Fast Saga, Wardriver), former Marvel Studios head Avi Arad, and Jessica Jones executive producer Karim Zreik. Mike Gamble was also involved, and this report suggests he still is, but it remains to be seen how his position on the project has changed with BioWare’s demise, given he served as a guiding voice from the studio. The Mass Effect series has no release window.

The Mass Effect series joins other video game adaptations Amazon has in the works, which include a third season of Fallout (with Aaron Paul joining the cast), a live-action God of War series starring Dave Bautista, a live-action Tomb Raider series starring Sophie Turner, as well as series based on Life is Strange and Wolfenstein.

For more on Mass Effect, check out our review of the Legendary Edition and our recently republished Oral History of BioWare from 2016.
