#4278. Aether Gazer tier list - Jade Forger - Vulu included

Our Aether Gazer tier list is specially created for perfectionists and theory-crafting admins looking for a one-stop guide to deck out your squad fully, or for love-struck admins wishing to bring out the best of their favourites, with so many maidens and blokes clad in exquisite futuristic suits to choose from.

To put an abrupt stop to your dilemma, we have put together an Aether Gazer tier list ranking each Modifier and measuring their overall performance for each part of the game, irrespective of their base ranks. Here’s how it works - each modifier stands a chance to fully realise its potential through Transcendence to the famed Omega rank. In addition, the term Omega is also commonly applied to a combo streak. It is denoted by the letters appearing at the upper left side of the corner that slowly build up as your characters attack.

Now, click on the big blue button, and let's head right into Modifier rankings.

The real-deal elites, regardless of their shape and size, are the premier choice that you should throw your resources at whenever an opportunity arises. They are also the best choices for newbies to grasp the basics. As progression is timed by stamina, I'd encourage you to spend your hard-earned resources on them first. Fret not, as most in this category are obtainable from the starter’s pool.

We're starting off the Aether Gazer tier list with Tyr - he is a self-reliant powerhouse without needing to rely on signature Functors. He works exceptionally well even with a 4-star Functor or lower. His impressive stats provide him with enormous bulk, which can be left comfortably in the hands of AI while being able to dish out excellent damage to bosses and mobs. This is thanks to his skill, which enhances his damage percentage by the thousands (while most Modifiers have a ceiling of hundreds).

Ashura, the petite girl with the appetite of a glutton, is the top-tier fire-element damage dealer, and her position looks set to remain unchallenged for aeons to come. Her most unique calling card lies in her second skill, as she is the only modifier that can trigger a “Zero time” on demand. She is also capable of refreshing her skill cooldown with successful evades. The caveat is that she requires you to be hands-on. The AI simply isn't up to the task. Sakura, the rabbit-crazed maniac, is a top-tier team player as she is blessed with a competitive skill set that brings a plethora of buffs to the table, including a party-wide heal, attack up, pierce, and battery. Just like Tyr, she is already stellar without a signature functor. Her main mechanic as a berserker-type character is rage-inducing - she collects and deals high damage with a pretty important attribute called Divine Grace. Of course, her standout aspect stems from her first skill that randomly grants buffs (purple, yellow and green that bolster self-attack, gain rage points and self-heal). Unlike Rahu Asura, she is one of the best modifiers that has total compatibility with the AI. Artic Abyss is truly the cream of the crop of S rank modifiers - she is a support-oriented modifier who provides ample buffs to the team, and is known (and remains) to be the top-tier battery who provides Cooldown to skills and ultimates for your fellow allies, coupled with some healing and minor power-ups.

They are the second top brass - not the shiniest but their prowess is almost equivalent to the S tier. They are highly capable and robust in their own right. Here is where the majority of A-grade modifiers reside.

Starting this part with, Jin-ei, the one with unrivaled bodysuit appeal, is distinguished by being the jack of all elements and master of none thanks to her skill kit. Each of her skills allows her to deal with different kinds of elemental damage, making her a universal addition to the team. Sher will test enemy’s elemental disadvantages and fits in any element-themed team like a glove.

Moving on in the A rank echelon, we have The Innocence, a modifier shrouded with a meek veneer. Thanks to her damage-oriented kit, she can nearly match everyone here. Additionally, it is easy to max transcend her. Her skills allow her to easily solo bosses and wipe the floor with mobs.

The next A rank modifier is Gusty Lance, an operator who debriefs admins on their missions. She dual-wields combat lances and easily racks up damage by parrying while consistently dodging. On top of that, she easily draws out her strength without relying much on functors, much like Tyr.

Similarly, Frost Fang is an evasion-based modifier just like Gusty Lance. She can receive a good 50% boost to her ice elemental attacks for every successful evasion. She makes for a good boss killer as well as crowd control thanks to the incremental attack gain (up to 90% permanently during battle) granted by one of her skills.

This echelon mostly constitutes A-grade modifiers who fell short compared to the upper ranks, either overshadowed in terms of virtue or their niche involving high stakes. With that said, they can be serviceable to tackle most in-game content with subpar efficiency, provided they are given the proper nourishment.

While their abilities slightly pale in comparison to their peers in higher ranks, they are serviceable and can get through most content, provided they have higher transcendence and better gear investment. This is especially great as the majority of Modifiers here are A-rank modifiers, and so their shards are relatively easier to farm.

Starting with the lone wolf in the bunch, Ryugiri is a base S rank modifier on paper as he is a sturdy tank impervious to hitstun. Due to his expertise in wielding one-handed blades, he is suited to soloing enemy bosses. To achieve maximum efficiency, he requires a boatload of investment (access key functors, transcendence, and sigils) to be able to perform slightly below the strongest S rank modifiers. Above all, he requires the possession of very specific fire-type modifiers, as well as support within a team to fully drive out his potential.

Moving on to the second member of the icy pair, Drifting Flurry is a hybrid support tank modifier. Her standout trait is her skill that can invalidate boss units with crowd control effects that hinder modifiers. She shines perfectly in a full-fledged ice team and pairs well with Vidar.

Shinku is a modifier focused on dealing continuous damage and building up a combo streak. While her blade-slashing animations are flashy and gratifying, she is unfortunately hampered by very low damage output owing to the low damage percentage on all her skills, forcing her to rely on resource investment, particularly Sigils, to function properly. Radiant Feather can ensnare a group of mobs in one spot and apply a debuff that cripples the enemy's resistance to fire-type attacks. She is an ideal support for any fire team, but works exceptionally well with Ryugiri and Aigertlam. Sadly, that’s where her versatility ends. Nuasha stands out as a fire damage dealer with good AoE coverage, but his damage scales with how much damage he consistently takes. Though, as a countermeasure, he can recover a small portion of HP based on the damage he’s taken, branding him as a decent meat shield in a fire team.

This is also known as the "Never-Used" tier.

Just like many other gacha games, each newcomer is given a set of modifiers to unravel their tale. In Aether Gazer, the main “starter” is Verthandi. Her original base variant is less than useful in the long run and should only be used if you find her outspoken and cheerful personality endearing. However, further on in the game, she is poised to receive a new suit that makes her much more viable and feasible in the meta. Still, she can see some use in the early stages thanks to how easily you can stack her character shards for Transcendence.

Other candidates include the tag-along “starter” Surefire and the enigmatic Croc Rage. Surefire, sadly, is overshadowed in every way. Croc Rage, despite his ”hotheaded” banter, is mostly underwhelming with a suicide-happy skillset that takes effort to fully command his character. Some skills are unusable for bosses, though he can dispose of humanoid enemies that can be fulfilled by other modifiers. The sole A rank modifier in this list is The Glare. While his speciality is being able to leap back a distance by repeatedly spamming his second skill, he is hindered by his confusing skill kit and severely low damage output.

#4277. Jordan Esports Federation signs MoU with King Hussein Business Park to host more events

Priya Venkatesh has been following the money in esports since before brand deals were considered legitimate marketing. She got pulled into the scene through competitive fighting games and eventually found herself more interested in the contracts and partnerships behind the tournaments than the matches themselves. These days she focuses on how brands navigate esports sponsorships, where the smart money is going, and which deals are actually built to last versus the ones that look good in a press release.

The Jordan Esports Federation (JEF) has signed a memorandum of understanding with King Hussein Business Park (KHBP) in Amman, giving the national body a formal framework to stage more tournaments and events at the site it already calls home.

KHBP announced the deal on Sunday in a statement published on its website. Prince Omar bin Faisal, who is President of the JEF, attended the signing.

Under the MoU, the federation and the business park will jointly host and organise specialised competitions on the KHBP campus. They will also receive the international delegations and official guests that travel to those events. Beyond the competitive side, the two organisations plan to cooperate on media and marketing, look at shared education, training and community projects, and swap knowledge and expertise.

Neither party has disclosed financial terms or the length of the agreement.

KHBP CEO Eng. Ammar Ezzeddin presented the MoU as part of the park’s wider ambitions. “This partnership builds on our ongoing efforts to create an enabling environment for institutions, initiatives and high-potential sectors, and to establish KHBP as a hub for innovation and technology,” he said.

He added: “We look forward to helping the sector thrive and to hosting more tournaments and events that put Jordanian talent in the spotlight and raise the Kingdom’s profile in this field.”

JEF Vice President Hazem Bawab focused on the competitive and grassroots goals. “This partnership is a significant step in our drive to develop the esports industry in Jordan and elevate the standard of local, regional and international competitions and activities,” he said.

Bawab continued: “We look forward to drawing on the setup and capabilities that KHBP offers to scale our work, nurture young talent and launch joint programmes that help the industry grow and encourage greater participation.”

The deal formalises a relationship that already exists on the ground. According to The Esports Radar, the JEF, which is the government recognised regulator for esports in the country, is based at the park in West Amman.

A lot of that work happens at THE ARC, the arena and gaming dome inside the park. The same report lists past events there including the fourth Arab Esports League, a Women’s Esports Championship and Red Bull Login, which doubled as Jordan’s national final stage in Dota 2 and Counter-Strike 2. The venue is also an incubation centre supported by the federation and the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship, and runs training camps for players hoping to turn professional.

KHBP has been a destination for esports investment for some time. In 2024, lounge operator True Gamers announced plans for an esports venue in Jordan at the business park, a project in which its CPO publicly thanked the JEF and Prince Omar.

The timing also puts Amman in the industry spotlight. PocketGamer.biz points out that Pocket Gamer Connects Jordan takes place on 7 and 8 November, bringing many of the region’s games industry stakeholders to the city later this week.

#4276. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4275. Grammy Award-Winning Composer Austin Wintory Shares His Early Musical Drafts Intended For Mass Effect 5

Last week, EA shut down Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare, which resulted in the cancellation of the fifth Mass Effect game that was announced in 2020. As the fallout from this closure settles, famed video game composer Austin Wintory has shared that he'd been working on a potential soundtrack for the now-canceled game and has publicly released early versions of this score.

In a Bluesky thread, Wintory, who has composed soundtracks for games such as Journey, Sword of the Sea (for which he won a Grammy), Assassin’s Creed: Syndicate, and The Banner Saga trilogy, writes, “Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale, my all-time dream project. For the last couple years I'd been in discussion w/ BioWare & EA to take on the project & as part of that I wrote close to 20 minutes of music to explore where the franchise can go next, may as well share it!"

Wintory uploaded a 20-minute video consisting of eight tracks to his YouTube channel. The video begins with a message further elaborating on the partnership between BioWare, EA, and him. “For the past several years, I’d been in dialogue with people both at BioWare and EA to potentially jump into Mass Effect 5. As part of these conversations, I decided to surprise the team by writing/recording a gigantic love letter to the franchise, with my idea of where it can go next.”

Wintory adds that he composed the music in 2025 and that he “knew nothing” about what Mass Effect 5's story entailed when he did. As such, he describes the music as “narratively speculative.” He adds that this conceptual soundtrack was a direct homage to Jack Wall and Sam Hulick’s soundtrack on the first Mass Effect “while leaning even harder on true analog synths, and a more complex integration of the orchestra (almost akin to the hybrid nature of The Matrix),” he writes. Each music track features a message by Wintory explaining his inspiration for its production.

“Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss," Wintory writes in the video's description. "It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever. Thank you nonetheless to everyone at BioWare and EA's music department for gifting me the chance to dream in your sandbox. It was a privilege to do even that much.”

Wintory's music is the latest piece of potential Mass Effect 5 content to emerge since BioWare’s closure. A day after the shutdown announcement, an unreleased but reportedly legitimate cinematic trailer for the canceled Mass Effect leaked online.

#4270. Free-To-Play MOBA Pokémon Unite Is Shutting Down In March

The free-to-play MOBA Pokémon Unite will shut down in March, over five years after its 2021 launch. Although a gradual suspension of services begins today, fans will enjoy one last hurrah thanks to a big in-game event running for the remainder of the game’s lifecycle.

Launched in July 2021 for Switch before migrating to iOS and Android later that year, Pokémon Unite was billed as a friendlier take on the MOBA genre popularized by Dota 2 and League of Legends, thanks to its short matches (10 minutes) and simplified mechanics. Despite its initial popularity, the game is winding down and will go offline for good on March 23, 2027.

An End of Service notice on the game’s website reads,

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021. We would like to express our thanks to everyone by holding a special event until service ends. The Pokémon Unite Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament (an event for Pokémon Unite only) will also be held as previously announced. We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service. After service ends, the 'Pokémon Unite Game Content Guidelines for Online Platforms' will no longer be published or maintained, and we will no longer provide support regarding use of Pokémon Unite videos and images.”

As of today, in-game sales of Aeos gems and Unite Club memberships/renewals have been suspended. Existing Unite Club members will continue to use their benefits until the end of the membership period.

On November 12, an update will kick off the aforementioned final special event, where players can obtain items such as all Unite licenses and Holoware that have appeared in the game up to that point. A library feature will also be added, letting players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down on March 23. Those who don’t download the library feature before the shutdown date will not be able to get it afterward.

Qualifiers for the Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo Competitive tournament will take place as planned on December 5. After the game shuts down on March 23, players won't be able to log in to Pokémon Unite or play any battles. Only the library feature will remain accessible.

We enjoyed Pokémon Unite when it launched, with executive video editor Alex Van Aken scoring it an 8 out of 10 in his review, writing, “The game eats away the hours of my day as I reassuringly say to myself, 'Just one more match.' Battles play out with the spectacle that the Pokémon series is known for, and with so many abilities to choose from, no match feels the same as the last. The game’s simple mechanics and recognizable characters make for an approachable MOBA experience, and with a potential catalog of nearly 900 Pokémon to pick from, my hopes are high for the future of Pokémon Unite.”

#4269. KRÜ Blaze win Game Changers Championship from lower bracket, ending Gentle Mates’ unbeaten run

KRÜ Blaze came through the lower bracket to beat Europe's Gentle Mates GC over five maps in São Paulo, giving LATAM its first Game Changers Championship title. They are also the last winners of the standalone event, as next year's final moves to Champions.

KRÜ Blaze are the 2026 VALORANT Game Changers Championship winners. They edged Gentle Mates GC 3-2 at the Riot Games Arena in São Paulo on 1 November. No Latin American team had lifted the title before. No team had ever won it from the lower bracket either.

The event ran from 22 October, with 10 teams competing. Gentle Mates earned US$100,000 as runners-up. Shopify Rebellion Gold took US$70,000 for third place and MIBR GC US$50,000 for fourth.

KRÜ took the long route. They beat Gen.G GC 2-1 in the upper-bracket quarter-finals on 23 October. A 2-0 loss to Shopify Rebellion Gold on 27 October then dropped them into the lower bracket. They answered with clean sweeps of Team Liquid Brazil and MIBR GC. On 31 October they beat Shopify Rebellion Gold 3-1 in the best-of-five lower-bracket final.

The grand final swung back and forth. Gentle Mates took Haven 13-5 before KRÜ levelled on Abyss by the same score. KRÜ led the third map 10-2 at half-time. Gentle Mates fought back, but KRÜ closed it out 14-12 in overtime. Gentle Mates then won Split 13-8 to force a decider. KRÜ led 11-5 on Ascent and won it by the same margin as Split.

Liquipedia named KRÜ’s Argentine player tok1o as the event’s MVP. Brazilian teammates antG and none became the first Brazilians to win an international tournament held in São Paulo.

The result breaks a pattern. Before 2026 the title went to G2 Gozen for Europe in 2022, Shopify Rebellion for North America in 2023 and 2024, and Team Liquid Brazil in 2025. KRÜ’s own record at the event had improved steadily. They finished 7th–8th in 2022 and 5th–6th in each of the next two years. Last year they came fourth.

For European fans, it was a painful near miss. Gentle Mates GC arrived as EMEA’s top seed on circuit points. The team had not lost a series in São Paulo before the final, according to Esports News UK.

It capped a strong debut season in the circuit. Gentle Mates won EMEA Stage 1 by sweeping G2 Gozen 3-0 on 22 February. They lost the Stage 2 final to SK Nebula on 24 May without winning a map. On 30 August they lost the Stage 3 final to G2 Gozen in a fifth map. Silver in São Paulo leaves them with one title from four finals this year.

#4268. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4265. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4264. Roblox: Elemental Dungeons tier list - The Best (and worst) elements

An up-to-date Elemental Dungeons tier list after Update 9

Thanks to an ever-changing meta, creating an Elemental Dungeons tier list isn’t as easy as it is for most Roblox experiences. New elements get added regularly, and old ones are dumped into oblivion. On top of all that, elements getting nerfed or buffed in an update is quite common. While no one likes this much uncertainty surrounding one of the most important aspects of the game, it is what it is. Those who love crawling through the elemental dungeons have already made peace with it. So, it’s about time someone made an Elemental Dungeons elements tier list and kept it updated. Elemental Dungeons tier list explained After the latest update, there are 15 elements in Elemental Dungeons. We've ranked them into five different tiers, from tier S to tier D. The S tier is the strongest, while the D tier is for the weakest elements.

Check out our Elemental Dungeons guide for beginners to learn more about the Elements and how to use them. Our guide tells you how to obtain the Elements, use them effectively and get the best out of them. This tier list also tells you which elements are worth obtaining and upgrading.

With a new max mastery of 250, Angel has recently jumped from Epic to Legendary rarity. It is strong against Reaper, among others, and only weak against Lightning and Lava. It can deal massive AoE damage and heal nearby allies.

When an element is strong against EIGHT of the fifteen total elements, A tier is the least it deserves. Lightning is an Epic element that has been nerfed, nerfed, and nerfed, and yet still seems OP somehow. If it wasn’t for the nerfs, Lightning could have been in the S tier, but it still gives the Mythic and Legendary elements a run for their money. The damage-dealing abilities of this element are insane. Lightning is capable of destroying anything the game throws at you.

Light is an Epic tier element that was added to Elemental Dungeons with Update 1. It has 300 max mastery, and much like other elements, Light also has FIVE abilities. However, what sets Light apart is the fact that its third ability, Light Ray, and ultimate, Light Barrage, cast 16 ticks of damage while dealing three and four-figure damage per tick, respectively. Light is a decent substitute if you can’t get your hands on a Mythic element.

Ice is exactly what you’d expect from an Epic element. It does plenty of damage, but it is not overpowered. Ice can fight and destroy anyone and anything, but it’s hard work. Unlike the Mythic elements, you can’t one-shot anyone with Ice. But that doesn’t make it a bad element. Once you reach a good enough mastery level, you can spam an Ice Barrage and Ice Shuriken combo to deal massive damage that goes as high as 10,000+.

Although it is Legendary, Gravity doesn’t really belong in the Legendary tier. While I won’t tag it as the weakest Legendary element, it’s certainly not the strongest. The damage it deals is mediocre at best, but a couple of things are OP, which saved Gravity from falling to C tier. First is the seemingly unlimited range of the second skill, Meteor, and the second is the low cooldowns. Almost all of Gravity's skills become available within 5-10 seconds.

I’ll just say it. Air is a bad Rare element that’s pretty easy to get early. However, you should forget about it as soon as you get it. Fighting enemies with Air is hard, and fighting boss battles is even harder. The attacks are all over the place and miss the target half of the time. It’s only strong against elements that are weaker than Air.

Low damage, high AoE, strong against SIX elements but weak against SEVEN, Water is a weird element and not in a good way. Water is the only element whose strongest ability is the first. As you unlock Mastery Skills 2 and 3, the attack stats get lower and lower. It’s just not worth building on unless you’re really bored and are looking for a challenge.

That’s it for my Elemental Dungeons tier list. As the meta changes, which it surely will, I’ll make sure to update this tier list accordingly. Until then, have fun and keep an eye on similar content like ourAnime Dimensions tier list, thisBlade Ball ability tier list or ourUltimate Tower Defense tier list, to name a few that stand out.

#4262. Phantom Blade Zero Review – Wuxia Wonder Abounds

Rooted in Wuxian storytelling and scale, built on an impressively detailed combat system, and wrapped in a bloody Chinese martial underground that’s a genuine joy to play in, Phantom Blade Zero is a feat. It joins an echelon of action pedigree that includes Sekiro, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, and just about any other action game you hold in high regard. It hails from developer S-Game, which has dabbled in mobile and smaller-scale games, and I’m shocked by what it’s pulled off with its triple-A action inauguration. But make no mistake: though Phantom Blade Zero is this team’s first crack at a game like this, it is an incredibly confident, strong debut.

Protagonist Soul is a stoic martial arts master betrayed by the Order he’s sworn his life to; he dies and returns to life with only 66 days to live. That’s enough time to settle his debts, repay his betrayers, and end a villainous conspiracy to seize full power of the Wulin realm. This narrative is Phantom Blade Zero's weakest link, but its premise adds enough mystery and tension to keep this Wuxian journey exciting through to its final, realm-shattering moments. Narrative bombshells drop not just through the game’s general fantasy-realism art direction, but also through anime scenes, opera puppet shows, animated brushstroke sequences, and more, highlighting Chinese culture and its integral place in Phantom Blade Zero.

The game features a staggering number of unique enemy types, and though the final hours get a bit repetitive, it’s admirable how long S-Game maintains such a high level of combat-oriented ecstasy. Soul’s access to weapons drives that exhilaration. Every weapon is wholly unique. Because the combat is combo-based, picking up a new weapon feels like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. Each has its own moveset and abilities, with later-game weapons featuring combo lists that look more at home in a Street Fighter menu. Add in the special, tide-turning weapons known as Phantom Edges, with limited charge-based uses, and there’s no shortage of permutations to delightfully experiment with.

Drawing on Chinese cinema, Phantom Blade Zero's setpiece bosses boast a sense of awe and scale only the genre's best typically offer. With virtually no repeat bosses, save for a few in separate trials, it’s impressive how many powerful figures I flayed, and how many delivered a unique fight. I also appreciate the checkpoints between boss phases, as they remove the frustrating repetition of replaying phase one again and again just to take another stab at the second phase I’m struggling with.

You’d be forgiven for assuming Phantom Blade Zero is a Soulslike, given its challenging bosses, interconnected world, and Phantom Bell checkpoints, this game’s equivalent of bonfires. It definitively isn’t, though. The challenge is much more surmountable; the game isn’t interested in making you die over and over, there are difficulty options, and you can equip accessories to make parries and dodges easier. World progression is materially different, too, as enemies don’t respawn after you kill them. It’s an interesting, perhaps blasphemous, choice for the genre, but it's surprisingly effective, adding a sense of worldbuilding and tangible progression I didn’t know I wanted from my action games. Soul is on a mission to remove evil, and mechanically, I’m doing just that. Enemies don’t respawn incoherently just because I heal and save.

Environmental features weave in and out of each other, and the architectural design and layout of these regions lead to many subsequent “aha” moments. S-Game infuses search-action elements into this exploration through the aforementioned Phantom Edges, some of which double as tools to unlock surprising new areas in both new and previously visited biomes. As a result, backtracking and exploration remain fresh. A lot of it is optional, as are some of Phantom Blade Zero's most rewarding elements, including its demanding “perfect” ending. Sadly, this renders other endings unsatisfying, with clear chunks intentionally missing.

Despite forays into the Uncanny Valley, Phantom Blade Zero is visually striking, and the action is brilliantly animated. It’s all set to genre-breaking music, too, with original metalcore songs, operatic choirs, 808s, and traditional Chinese instrumentation, creating a score as illustrious as the action it enhances.

Phantom Blade Zero is an astounding action achievement, almost unbelievably so for a game that is essentially a studio’s genre debut. It is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, one that recognizes the genre’s strengths and weaknesses and addresses both with fantastical Wuxian style. Though the action genre is always jam-packed with new releases, few are as special as Phantom Blade Zero.

#4257. Fortnite Players are Scrambling for an Exceedingly Rare Treasure

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

In One Piece, the titular mysterious treasure left behind by the late Pirate King Gol D. Roger is said to be something of such unfathomable power, it could overturn everything people know about the world itself. Over 20 years later, we still don’t know what the One Piece actually is, but there have certainly been more than a few treasure hunts inspired by its legendary mystique. Rather fittingly, one of those treasures has manifested in the midst of Fortnite’s newest pirate-themed mini-season, and it's driving the internet bonkers.

On Sunday, following the end of the Fortnitemares Halloween event, Fortnite began an interstitial mini-season to tide players over until the next major content drop in December. This mini-season, Treasure Hunters, is most predominantly One Piece-themed, featuring a new map with various One Piece locales and a handful of One Piece characters in the shop and Battle Pass.

The people gave Sweeney and Epic all the attention and support it needed when it rose up to Apple. As a reward, players got a significant price hike.

However, in addition to that, outside of the actual announcements, a new element has been quietly added to the game, and following its discovery by the playerbase, a mad scramble to locate it on par with One Piece’s own Great Age of Piracy has begun. Players have set sail from all over in search of the Pirate Shop Token, the treasure that will make their (cosmetic-centric) dreams come true.

The Pirate Shop Token is a new item that has begun spawning in chests on the new map during Fortnite's pirate-themed Treasure Hunters mini-season. To put it succinctly, obtaining the Pirate Shop Token is a free pass to almost everything in the Fortnite shop.

Obtaining the Pirate Shop Token is a free pass to almost everything in the Fortnite shop.

If you happen to obtain the token, as the game will inform you after the fact, you can activate it at any time until its expiration on December 16, 2026. When the token is activated, any item in the Fortnite shop will become free to claim, even if you don’t have a single V-Buck to your name. From pickaxes to outfits to gliders, it’s all fair game. Not only that, but from the moment of activation, the Pirate Shop Token remains in effect for two weeks, which means you can keep helping yourself to the shop’s contents day after day until it expires. You’ll also receive a second token that can be activated at a currently-indeterminate point in 2027.

Following the arrest of a featured artist, Fortnite is allowing players to refund associated cosmetics.

There are some caveats here: real money offers, gifting and passes levels and rewards are excluded, and you can only claim one free sidekick that you don’t already own. Beyond those few bits, though, the rest is plunderable. We’re talking cumulative values in the hundreds of dollars in assorted cosmetics here, and suffice to say, a lot of people would very much like that.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, such a fabulous treasure isn’t going to be easy to find. The only way to obtain the Pirate Shop Token is to find it on the map after it randomly spawns in, for which there is no particular indication or notification. The actual odds of this spawn occurring are a black box secret held by Epic, though some rumors have circulated that they’re in the ballpark of 1 in 700,000. There have also been rumors that you’re more likely to find it if you’re lower-leveled, but these are probably bunk.

The only tangible thing you can do to improve your odds is grouping up. If one player in a party finds the token, everyone in the party gets it. This has sparked a new wave of mercenaries in the Fortnite community, with players offering their services to others to party up and systematically sweep the island for its chests in the hopes of finding a token.

On a less savory note, some users with alleged Pirate Shop Token access have begun attempting to sell their accounts on eBay, with proposed prices in the thousands, while others have attempted to circulate cheating tools to fudge the spawn rates. Epic issued a statement on these practices via the Fortnite Status X, formerly Twitter page, writing, “Buying an account or using fake tools is a scam. This is just like any of the chests in Battle Royale, so every player has an equal opportunity to find Pirate Shop Access.” Buying and selling Fortnite accounts is also a bannable offense, so don’t do that.

The group is seeking over €100 million in combined refunds and damages on behalf of underage players.

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

From one of the co-creators of Celeste, City of None has a gorgeous pixelated art style and colors that immediately remind me of Game Boy Color classics. It's a 2D platformer where you leap around, fight enemies, and explore the strange city around you. The jumping and fighting look solid, and I really like the mysterious atmosphere and art direction. City of None's set for sometime in 2027.

The sword-surfing adventure from the makers of Abzu and Journey is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on October 29, 2026 - tomorrow! It's a gorgeous adventure that earned a Must-Play badge from us, so it's worth your time if you like the kinds of gorgeous, beautiful adventures Giant Squid (developer of Abzu) is known for.

Take an overhead camera angle, brawler gameplay, and some John Wick sensibilities, and you've got Tenjutsu, a stylish roguelike where you use your martial arts prowess to tear apart crime syndicates. I really enjoy the look and vibe of this one, and it's from one of the designers of Dead Cells, too. Tenjutsu might be one to keep an eye on when it arrives on Switch 2 in 2027.

RPG fans have been eating well, and it looks like the feast could continue next year with Threads of Time. The time-traveling RPG is coming to both Switch and Switch 2 next summer, and it's looking absolutely gorgeous.

Ah, raccoons. Nature's most adorable little scamps. If you and your friends have ever wanted to live out the dream of being a rambunctious band of raccoons wreaking havoc on the town, Dumpster Gang sets out to give you just that fantasy in March 2027.

I've already enjoyed quite a bit of Super Battle Golf on PC, so I'll tell you now: if you enjoy golf games and want some Mario Party annoy-your-friends antics wound around them, Super Battle Golf should be on your radar for its March 25, 2027 launch on Switch 2.

Another port of a PC multiplayer mainstay, the co-op physics-driven horror-looter R.E.P.O. is coming to Switch 2 in 2027. This is one for the crowd that likes to be scared one moment and laughing hysterically the next.

Rounding out the co-op section, Haunted Paws has you and a pal playing as a pair of pups searching for their person in a haunted mansion. The side-scrolling 3D look makes it seem like a less-scary Little Nightmares, and the concept is pretty fun. Look for this one on Switch and Switch 2 in May 2027, or try out the free demo later today.

Enjoy shrines, towns, and strange night-time journeys into the unknown? Follow a fox girl and her frog friend on an adventure through a strange island in Kitsune: The Journey of Adashino on Switch 2 and Switch in spring 2027. I've said it a few times in this recap, but wow, the art here is great.

The second entry in the slime-collecting, home-building sim adventure is coming to Switch 2. Pick up adorable slimes with your vacuum, build a home for them, and explore the Rainbow Island around you in January 2027. Plus, there's an exclusive in-game item for the Switch 2 version.

From the makers of Cozy Grove, this multiplayer game encourages players to build a home above the clouds with friends and explore the world around them. Spirit Crossing looks like a big world to make your own alongside your pals, starting November 16, 2026 on both Switch and Switch 2.

Want something a little sillier? My Arms Are Longer Now is a game about, well, really long arms. With numerous Australian comedians lending their vocal talents to the project, this seems like it could be a quirky, charming, and delightfully funny experience when it arrives on both Switch and Switch 2 on March 11, 2027.

The chaotic coin-pushing game Raccoin is coming to Nintendo Switch 2. It's just like those token-shoving games you remember from arcades but with a number of wild and wacky means of pushing even more coins over the edge run-over-run. Raccoin: Chaos Max Edition hits Switch 2 on November 10, 2026, and a free demo is out later today.

#4252. Overwatch Isn't Slowing Down After Its 10th Anniversary

I spoke with Overwatch game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson about the game's future.

If 2026 had a defining trait for Overwatch, it was ambition. Celebrating its 10th anniversary, Blizzard's hero shooter went bigger than ever, dropping five new heroes at the start of the year and introducing a year-long narrative with The Reign of Talon. With Season 5 bringing that story to a close, it's fascinating to think how Blizzard can possibly top itself.

The good news is, the team isn't particularly interested in playing it safe. During a recent group interview I attended with game director Aaron Keller and associate game director Alec Dawson, I got a glimpse of what the next chapter looks like. While the developers aren't ready to spill all their secrets ahead of February's Overwatch Spotlight, there's already a clear message: 2027 won't simply be a repeat of 2026.

"We don't want players to feel like there is this tight playbook that we're following every year," Keller says. The team still wants to deliver a major annual release, but keeping players guessing is part of the appeal. "Yes, every year we do want to release something big," he says, teasing a February expansion that has been in development for quite some time.

Overwatch has spent the past two years focusing on Perks, Stadium, new heroes, and a renewed attention to storytelling. Though there's a difference between maintaining that momentum and making every update that follows an increasingly cool spectacle.

For Dawson, the answer is knowing when to add something new and when to take a step back. "We're curators and also caretakers at the same time," he says. The team wants to introduce new experiences, but it's equally important to make sure existing systems are healthy. That means paying attention to progression, balance, and the smaller improvements that might not generate a Twitter-breaking announcement, but make a difference to the people logging in every day.

Perhaps the biggest change this year has been seeing Overwatch commit to a continuous narrative again. The Reign of Talon gave us an entire year to follow Vendetta's rise, Doomfist's downfall, and the shifting relationships between the game's growing cast of heroes. Best of all, Blizzard has no intention of putting the comics away just yet.

"I'm so excited for the 2027 story that's going to be coming out," Keller says. In fact, he believes the next opening cinematic could be the best the team has ever produced.

The upcoming Season 6 hero trailer will also serve as the prologue to that next narrative, which will lay the groundwork for what's coming. Keller says the team is investing even more in storytelling next year, although there's some room for improvement in how it delivers that content.

One problem is that Overwatch's story can be easy to miss. From cinematics, motion comics, smaller character-focused stories, and Webtoon releases, keeping up can sometimes feel like a chore. Even players who enjoy the lore might not know where to look for the next piece.

Keller acknowledges that the team needs to make its narrative more accessible, while Dawson wants individual story arcs to feel more connected to the world around them. It's not enough for one storyline to end and another to begin; the events in between should have consequences.

That's exciting for longtime fans who have spent years waiting for certain character relationships and unfinished storylines to receive some attention. Keller even hints that 2027's narrative will revisit previously established material rather than starting completely from scratch.

For all the new heroes, narrative developments, and experimental modes, Keller and Dawson are conscious that Overwatch can't simply keep adding things forever. With 2026 adding an unprecedented number of new characters, the team is already thinking about how to keep the experience readable and welcoming to newcomers.

"We're not there yet," Keller says of the point where the roster might become too large to sustain the current release pace. Still, it's something the developers discuss internally.

That's the most interesting takeaway from our conversation. Blizzard isn't treating Overwatch's 10th anniversary as an excuse to coast on nostalgia. It wants to keep experimenting, but it also seems increasingly aware that the game's future depends on knowing which experiments are worth keeping.

The next Overwatch Spotlight will come in February 2027, and there are promises of another huge expansion. Keller isn't ready to reveal exactly what's coming, but he is making one thing super clear: Team 4 wants to surprise players rather than just continue to follow last year's formula.

After a decade of reinventions, cancellations, comebacks, and more than a few community arguments, Overwatch is heading into its next chapter with plenty left to prove. Fortunately, it sounds like Blizzard isn't running out of ideas just yet.

#4250. 8 JRPGs That Came Back From the Dead

Murillo Zerbinatto is a JRPG enthusiast, writer, and editor. He has played over 300 RPGs during his gaming career, with 90% of them being JRPGs.

It feels like we have been living through a game renaissance for quite some time. While development costs continue to inflate, particularly in the Western market, one way to keep the fanbase engaged with a developer and its IPs is to bet on smaller games, or even on ports, remasters, and remakes.

Another approach is to play on older fans' nostalgia, investing in older IPs while modernizing certain titles to attract newcomers at the same time. One genre that does this frequently is JRPGs, and as you can see in the following list, there are several JRPGs that pretty much came back from the dead, titles that had not shown their face in years and returned either as a remake or a brand new entry.

When Square Enix started with their HD-2D games, it was pure happiness. A rescue of the pixel art that the developer understands so well, but better than ever, paired with traditional gameplay. What I didn't expect, and I think nobody did, was that they would leverage this graphical engine to remake some older titles, and among these, Live A Live.

Live A Live was a JRPG released in 1994 for the Super Famicom exclusively in Japan, so imagine everyone's surprise when a modern remake was announced for 2022. Seriously, no one could have expected that. But there is a good reason, and aptly so, why Live A Live is timeless and was so well received by the modern audience 28 years after its original release.

Lunar was one of the JRPGs Game Arts released for the Sega CD, and it quickly earned a reputation as one of the finest JRPGs of the fourth generation. The first two mainline entries also quickly followed on PS1, reaching a much larger audience and becoming classic titles for the console. Portables followed, including Lunar Legend and the critically offensive Lunar Dragon Song.

In 2009, the series tried a comeback with Lunar: Silver Star Harmony, a remake of the first game for the PSP, and while critics loved it, it didn't give the franchise a second wind. Well, me, you, and our moms thought Lunar was over. But then, out of nowhere, GungHo announced Lunar Remastered Collection, a compilation of Lunar: Silver Star Story Complete and Lunar 2: Eternal Blue Complete, bringing the franchise back after 26 years without a sign of life.

Nihon Falcom is really focusing its efforts on bringing its entire lineup to modern platforms.

NISA is one of the oldest Japanese developers around, but the studio really found its footing after releasing the tactical La Pucelle: Tactics. It went on to mimic that gameplay style across several other franchises, mainly the well-known Disgaea. In 2004, it released Phantom Brave, another tactical JRPG following the same NISA blueprint, but with its own distinct identity and slightly different gameplay.

Phantom Brave was a solid game. I enjoyed it, but I really thought it was a one-and-done deal. I was pretty surprised when NISA announced Phantom Brave: The Lost Hero, not only a game set in the same universe, but a direct narrative sequel. Okay, luckily the game included a recap because releasing a sequel to a 20-year-old game was wild, but it is what it is.

I have mentioned Brigandine a few times here on the site, including in my review of Brigandine Abyss. I discovered this franchise serendipitously, and it took a long time to find other people who were also familiar with it. Truth be told, I only found them when I started frequenting the depths of Reddit. I had even forgotten about it, only to be reminded when I stumbled upon Brigandine: The Legend of Runersia.

Reviving an old IP or a cult classic happens every now and then, as you can see with other titles here. But Brigandine was not a cult hit, a classic, or even mildly famous. It was obscure among obscure titles, so why Happinet thought of bringing it back baffles me, but they did. Brigandine: The Legend of Forsena came out in 1998 and Runersia in 2020. The game apparently did well enough to warrant a new mainline entry, Brigandine Abyss, released just this year.

There are more than a few JRPGs that are still stuck on older systems and deserve a port to modern platforms.

I have always preferred fantasy games over sci-fi, but if there was one franchise where mechas stole my heart, or in this case, Wanzers, it was Front Mission. I played and replayed Front Mission 3 so many times and never grew tired of it, especially since the game featured branching narrative paths and a degree of RNG when learning skills, making every playthrough feel fresh. Then came the fourth mainline entry, Scars of War, Front Mission Evolved, and ugh, Left Alive, which come on, is not a Front Mission game, so let us dismiss it.

Well, in 2020, Forever Entertainment said it was working on a remake of an established Square Enix franchise that had multiple releases. My guess was either Parasite Eve or Front Mission, and since the former is tied up in licensing issues, yeah, it was Front Mission. The first remake launched in 2022, the second in 2023, and the third in 2025. I don't know if the franchise will continue, but it was great to revisit it through modern releases.

I know this entry is a bit far-fetched and even a tad insulting. After all, calling Valkyrie Elysium a mainline Valkyrie Profile entry is a stretch, but closing our eyes doesn't make it less true. After years without a new entry, Valkyrie Elysium was announced and left many fans excited, especially the nostalgic ones who adored the mysterious adventures of Lenneth back on the PS1.

What we got, however, wasn't what we wanted. It is not a bad game per se. It's just too middle-of-the-road and doesn't reflect what Valkyrie Profile represented, whether in the first game, Silmeria, or even Covenant of the Plume. Still, Valkyrie Elysium arrived in 2022, 13 years after the last mainline entry, so it fits the topic. I'm also not considering the mobile game Valkyrie Anatomia.

The producer is giving us hope, or at least some more coping issues.

Mana was always such a cozy, colorful, and friendly series. I loved playing Secret of Mana with my brother or transferring my character from Legend of Mana onto a memory card to bring to my friend's house. Good times. Even so, for one reason or another, it never achieved massive mainstream success. In 2007, Heroes of Mana came out for the Nintendo DS, followed in 2014 by Rise of Mana, a mobile-first game that received a Vita port. It was an oddity.

The franchise faded for a bit, but returned with the remake Adventures of Mana, followed by Secret of Mana and then Trials of Mana. The success of the remakes, especially Trials, signaled something to Square Enix, because it didn't take long for them to produce a brand-new mainline title in Visions of Mana. Personally, I loved Visions! It was a modernized version of everything I liked about Mana. I don't know why the game didn't achieve the success it deserved, but it may have been the last time we saw a mainline Mana entry.

You have probably heard someone say that Suikoden II is their favorite JRPG of all time. It was one of the most remarkable titles on the PS1 and built a deeply dedicated fanbase. Three more mainline entries later, the series began to fade into oblivion, still receiving a few spinoffs like Suikoden Tierkreis in 2009 and the Japan-only Gensō Suikoden: Tsumugareshi Hyakunen no Toki in 2012, which was its latest release. It was a strange era for both the series and Konami, which had stepped away from the video game industry for a while.

Then, completely out of nowhere, Konami announced Suikoden I & II HD Remaster: Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars during Tokyo Game Show 2022. It was a pleasant surprise, made even sweeter with the arrival of Suikoden Star Leap, which released in 2026. And okay, I know it is a mobile game, but those who played it (still locked in Japan) say it feels like a full-fledged Suikoden game, so who knows, maybe this will convince Konami to produce an offline version of Star Leap or a brand-new mainline entry altogether.

The GOG Dreamlist aims to preserve classic games. Here are 10 JRPGs that I would love to see on the platform, and they just need your vote.

Share your take with fellow players. Keep it constructive, relevant, and respectful.

#4248. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4244. Monsta brings a turn-based portable classic to mobile, where it's you versus mutant monsters

For many of us, the history of mobile gaming only stretches back to the first iPhone, and maybe a little further if we head back to the days of flip phones and the N-Gage. But look even further back, to when PDAs (Personal Digital Assistants) were all the craze, and you'll find examples of the primordial soup of mobile gaming, such as Monsta.

First released back in the 2000s on PalmOS devices, and now available for the modern-day iOS and Android platforms, Monsta had to tackle many hardware limitations, including slow processing speed at the time. That's what inspired developer Superverse Industries to create this turn-based tactical shooter, where it's just you and a building full of monsters to get before they get you.

You'll need to plan your moves, make use of various gadgets and weapons, and deal with monsters boasting their own distinct and deadly abilities.

And more than that, the gameplay itself has also looped round from being simplified for the purpose of dealing with limited performance, to stepping into the same trend of turn-based, roguelike(ish) games that have conquered the market recently.

All this and a who's who of artists, developers and composers from that particular slice of early 2000s Serbian game development makes Monsta a game worth checking out for its historical value, if nothing else. But with over 50 handmade levels, multiple upgrades and monsters to fight off, Monsta is worth checking out as a game on its own merits!

In the meantime, if you find yourself wanting a blast from the past like Monsta just a little more, why not check out our list of the best retro-inspired games on iOS for some choice picks?
