#4243. Where To Find All Pieces Of Heart In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake boasts quite a few collectibles to find throughout Hyrule. From Gold Skulltula to bag upgrades to three different elemental arrows, these can all help you make your life a little easier when facing off against the forces of Ganondorf.

Perhaps the most important item to find is the 36 Pieces of Heart, which will raise Link's overall health, making him much harder to put down. However, many of these aren't easily found and will require a bit of legwork. Additionally, several of these will be in brand new locations, so even if you're an Ocarina of Time veteran, you won't always be able to rely on your past experiences.

Here is where to find all the Pieces of Heart in the Ocarina of Time remake.

Some quick information before we get to the actual locations. The first thing is this list will not cover the full Heart Containers you get after defeating every major boss. They are basically unmissable and act as rewards for finishing a dungeon. Additionally, this list will be in chronological order, meaning, this is the order you can unlock them as you play the game.

Because of this, I recommend bookmarking this guide and using it as a reference for when you play. That way, as you progress through the story, you can grab every Piece of Heart available in that moment.

Your first Piece of Heart can be found at Lon Lon Ranch in the middle of Hyrule Field. When you arrive at the ranch, head to the back right corner where the large, partially destroyed stone tower is. Inside, there will be several crates you need to move, so shift them around so the middle one and one on the left that are closest to the metal bars are pulled away. This lets you crawl into the hole and reach the Heart Piece on the other side of the tunnel.

Kakariko Graveyard (Night) — Dampe's Graveyard Mini-Game

In the graveyard at night, talk to Dampe while he is roaming around to play the Graveyard Tour game. For this, you will need to pay him 10 Rupees to dig out one of eleven possible spots around the graveyard. Unfortunately, the Piece of Heart is entirely randomized, so you cannot reliably always pick the same location. Thankfully, you can always save, pick a spot, and if it's not right, reload the save and try again. You're looking for a dig spot that is hardened, requiring you to pay Dampe a second time. Sadly, this also isn't always a guarantee, but it's what you're looking for.

Kakariko Graveyard (Night) — Under The Tombstone

Staying in the graveyard, you can find the next Heart Piece by moving the farthest tombstone on the right in the second row all the way back. This will reveal a hole you can jump down into where you'll find a big chest with a Heart Piece inside.

You can get this Piece of Heart once you've obtained the Fairy Ocarina, but it's easier to just get it once you've been tasked with learning Saria's Song. Upon entering the Lost Woods via the Kokiri Forest entrance, hang a right to enter an area with a target hanging from a tree. Go down the ladder to the lower level and step onto the tree stump in front of the two Skull Kids. You will now need to complete three games of Simon Says, where you repeat on your ocarina what they play on their flutes.

The next Piece of Heart in the Lost Woods can be obtained right after you get Saria's Song. Once you have learned this tune, from the Kokiri Forest entrance, go left through the large hole to the left to find a long Skull Kid sitting on a tree in front of an empty tree stump. Climb onto the tree stump, take out your Fairy Ocarina, and play Saria's Song.

Your next Heart Piece can be acquired after you've received the Goron Bracelet from Darunia. Now that you can pick up Bomb Flowers, take out your Deku Stick and use it to light the torches around the massive vase at the bottom floor of the city. This will cause the vase to start spinning around on its platform. Now go to the next floor and grab the Bomb Flow in the back left corner by the mural of dancing Gorons (circled in the photo). Quickly run over to the edge and throw the Bomb Flower into the top of the vase. If you can get the Bomb Flower to explode while inside the vase, it will spit out a Piece of Heart.

Death Mountain Crater — Near The Entrance

Obtainable after you've beaten Dodongo's Cavern, this Piece of Heart is located at the very top of Death Mountain. Head up the mountain, and when you reach the massive opening, make sure you are at full health before heading inside. You'll have a very short time before you burn to death, so the moment you enter, sprint for the netting hanging over the edge of the cliffs on the left. Climb down the netting, and at the bottom will be the Heart Piece. This will fully restore your health, so quickly climb back up and run out!

One of the easiest in the game to miss, this Piece of Heart can only be found as Young Link in Death Mountain Crater. From the entrance, head left and down to the lower level that's to the right of the bombable hole in the ground. There you will find a Business Scrub who attacks when you're near. Use a Deku Nut to stun him and then hit him once. He will apologize for being so aggressive and will sell you a Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees. Again, remember that this can only be done as Young Link, which means you'll be taking damage this whole time so move fast!

You can get the next Piece of Heart immediately after obtaining the one in Death Mountain Crater. Upon exiting the crater, talk to the large owl, Kaepora, and ask him to bring you to the base of the mountain. After a brief cutscene, he will drop you off on a roof in Kakoriko Village. Go to the back left corner of the roof and look down at the stables. There will be a Piece of Heart on the red roof you can jump to!

Hyrule Castle Town — Bombchu Bowling Alley

Now that we have Bombs, the Bombchu Bowling Alley has officially opened in Hyrule Castle Town. When you arrive in town, go to the square and enter the parlor on the left. Talk to the vendor to play the game, which requires you to destroy three yellow targets with the Bombchus you're supplied. There are three difficulty levels to this mini-game, and you'll need to beat all of them to unlock the Piece of Heart. This is pretty easy, as you don't have a time limit and will have way more bombs than you need. Don't be afraid to destroy the obstacles, as this will use a bomb, but it makes hitting any target behind it way easier!

You can get another Piece of Heart in town, but you can only do it at night. Once the sun is down, look for the larger woman crying by the town entrance. Speak to her to learn that her dog, Richard, has run off, and she wants you to find it. You'll notice there are a ton of stray dogs running around town, so this seems like a difficult task. Thankfully, we know that Richard is colored white, which heavily limits which dog he is. Go down the alley on the left and interact with the first white dog you find to make it follow you. Bring this back to the woman to learn if it's Richard or not. If it is, you'll get a Piece of Heart; if not, you'll need to go find a different white dog. This is very much trial and error, so it may take a few attempts until you bring over the correct dog.

With our business concluded in Castle Town, make your way to Gerudo Valley, which is to the west in Hyrule Fields. When you arrive, grab the Cucco then walk to the left of the suspension bridge. You will see a chest on a cliff across the gap below you. While holding the Cucco, jump off and use it to float across the ravine. Drop the chicken near the chest and open it to get a Piece of Heart!

Gerudo Valley — Gerudo Valley Entrance Waterfall

Staying in Gerudo Valley, take the Cucco and take it back to where the suspension bridge is. Jump off the cliff while holding the bird and float down towards the massive waterfall on the right. When you land in the water, climb onto the nearby path and then head towards the waterfall. You will find a series of stone stairs behind this waterfall that leads to a small opening where the Piece of Heart can be found.

For this Piece of Heart, you need to catch a fish that is 58cm or bigger at the Fishing Pond. Found on the west side of Lake Hylia. Talk to the owner of the Fishing Pond about renting a fishing rod, and then try to cast your lure near the center of the watering hole. You're specifically looking for a large green fish, as that's the one I caught that earned me the Piece of Heart. This may take a few attempts, but there's no time limit, and you can use the fishing rod as much as you want once it has been rented. Just keep aiming for the bigger, bright green fish, and you'll snag one that's the right size. Once you do, return to the vendor and give him your fish to earn your prize.

The first Piece of Heart in Zora's River can be found roughly halfway up the river. When you arrive, progress upstream until you can go behind the locked gate where the Magic Bean Salesman is sitting in front of you. Behind it will be a Cucco, so grab that and carry it up the river until you reach an area with two Blue Tektites. Throw the bird onto the path in front, kill the bugs, and then pick it back up. Now, don't go upstream anymore; instead use the Cucco to fly across the gap to the south. Release the bird, climb the vines, and then head to the small area you need to reach via a small jump to the south. There you'll find a hole; go into the hole, grab the Cucco, and return to the surface. Finally, use that Cucco to reach the Piece of Heart on the elevated rocky platform.

The next Piece of Heart is close by and doesn't require nearly as much work. This time, take a Cucco all the way to the end of the river. On the north side, at the start of the river, you will see a small cliff where the Heart Piece resides. Use the Cucco to jump and cross the gap to obtain this upgrade.

The only Piece of Heart in Zora Domain is obtained by lighting all the unlit torches in the area. You start at the top where King Zora is and will work your way down the stairs and under the waterfall where you practice diving and earn the Silver Scale item. Once all the torches are lit, a large chest will appear with the Heart Piece inside.

This Piece of Heart can be found in the Kakariko Graveyard on the left. Assuming you planted a Magic Bean into the Bug Hole on the left, you can now find a large flower that Link can ride in the future. Step onto the flower, let it raise you up to the ruins and grab the Piece of Heart on the pedestal.

After beating Dampe in a race and unlocking the Hookshot, follow the path up the ruined stairs. Use the Hookshot to cross the gap, which will spit you out in Kakariko Village's windmill. Now carefully walk onto the rotating platform and ride it over to the next Heart Piece.

The next Piece of Heart can be acquired by completing Dampe's Race a second time and reaching the finish line in under a minute. This isn't as difficult as it sounds thanks to the new sprint button. The trick here is to never stop running, cut as many corners as you can, and do not get hit once by his fire. Getting struck by his flames can end your entire attempt, so always stick towards the walls, as Dampe rarely throws his flames right next to them. Also, you may run past a ReDead, but do not stop or even give it a chance to stun you! Beat Dampe in under a minute and the Piece of Heart is yours.

Now that we have the Hookshot, we can get onto the roof of the Potion Shop and talk to the man on it. Go up toward the gate to Death Mountain Trail and enter the Potion Shop on the right. Use the back door behind the counter to the left and then look to the other Potion Shop's roof on the right. Aim the Hookshot at the vines to pull you onto the roof. Talk to the man sitting there to earn a Heart Piece.

Back at Lake Hylia, if you planted a Magic Bean, you can step onto the large flower right next to the Lakeside Laboratory entrance. Ride the flower around Lake Hylia and jump off when it reaches the top of the Laboratory. Climb up the tower to find a Piece of Heart at the top.

Lake Hylia — Lakeside Laboratory Interior

To get this Piece of Heart you will need to get the Golden Scale. This is done by first beating the fish record as Young Link to earn a Piece of Heart and then doing it a second time as Adult Link. Remember, to reach the Fishing Pond in the future, you need to ride the Magic Bean Flower and jump off when it passes by. Once you have the Golden Scale, go into the laboratory, jump into the dive tank, and swim all the way to the bottom. Touch the floor underwater, then return to the surface. The Lake Scientist will be impressed with your skills and give you a Piece of Heart.

Your next Gold Skulltula is located in the Skulltula House. Once you've collected 50 Gold Skulltulas, you can visit this location in Kakariko Village and talk to them to earn a Piece of Heart. This only works if you get 50 Gold Skultulas, so make sure to use our guide if you are missing some!

Go back in the past once you learn the Song of Storms and at least five other songs. Once you have enough tunes, go to Zora River and look for the five colored frogs along the northern wall about halfway through this area. Play five different songs, not including the Song of Storms, to cause them all to grow. After making them grow, play the Song of Storms to cause it to rain earning you a Piece of Heart.

Stay at the frogs and listen as they offer to play a mini-game with you. You will need to play specific notes on your ocarina to make the frog with the spotlight on them jump up to catch the butterfly above them. Every frog has a corresponding button on your controller. Light Blue is L, Yellow is R, Dark Blue is Y, Grey is X, and Red is A. Complete the full mini-game with no mistakes to earn a Piece of Heart.

If you planted a Magic Bean in the soft soil spot right outside of Dodongo's Cavern, you will find a Magic Bean Flower. Step onto the flower to ride it up to the opening in the mountain directly above the dungeon entrance. There you will find your next Piece of Heart.

Death Mountain Crater — Magic Bean Flower

For this Piece of Heart, progress through the story until you learn the Bolero of Fire from Shiek. Once this happens, warp back to the Temple of Time and swap to young Link. Now, get a Magic Bean and a bug in a bottle. Play the Bolero of Fire and teleport there as a kid. You won't have much time, so quickly look for the bug hole right by the warp point. Use the bug to coax out a Gold Skulltula, kill it, then plant a Magic Bean in the soil. Teleport back to the Temple of Time, switch to adult Link, then finally return to the Fire Temple entrance. Step on the Magic Bean Flower and ride it to the next Piece of Heart.

This one is a little weird to get. First go towards Gerudo Valley in the west and head underneath the large stone arch on the right. Underneath, you will find an open chest, along with a Fairy Note on the wall. Read the note to learn that they unlocked the chest, but someone stole the Piece of Heart. Now, return to the past and visit this exact same spot as young Link. This time, you will find the chest unlocked, but still closed. Open the chest to get your Heart Piece.

Hyrule Field — Outside Hyrule Castle Town

I'm putting this here solely because my dumbass missed it and only discovered it a bit later. There's a chance you can absolutely get this as early as gaining the ability to go back and forth between time. To the right of the drawbridge outside of Hyrule Castle Town, along the stone wall, you will find a bombable patch of land. Going down the hole, you'll find a Business Scrub who will only sell items if you know the password. Go back up and look for a tree nearby that has a Fairy Thought carved into it. Reading it you will learn that the password is "Sell somethin', will ya?" Unfortunately, the future Business Scrub has already sold his Piece of Heart. Go back in time and return to this Business Scrub as young Link. Talk to him again and give the vendor the right password. You can now buy the Piece of Heart for 100 Rupees.

When you arrive at Zora Fountain as adult Link, you will find that Lord Jabu-Jabu is gone and there is ice everywhere. In the northeast corner of this area there will be several icy platforms that you can jump across to reach a Piece of Heart at the end. Just be careful, as there are Octoroks ready to attack along the path. Take your time crossing, and you'll easily snag this Heart Piece.

After completing the Ice Cavern, take some Blue Fire to King Zora to thaw him out of the ice. He will give you the Zora Tunic, allowing you to breathe underwater. Return to Zora Fountain and use the Iron Boots in combination with your new threads to sink to the bottom where the Piece of Heart is surrounded by a ring of Rupees.

Hyrule Castle Town — Treasure Chest Mini-Game

Once you unlock the Leneses of Truth, return to Hyrule Castle Town and head to the east. Look for the shop with the giant treasure chest above the door. Go inside and agree to play the mini-game. In each room, there will be two treasure chests, one of which has a Small Key inside. Use the Leneses to figure out which chest has the key, allowing you to progress to the next room. Do this five times, and the Piece of Heart is yours.

The next Piece of Heart is located at Gerudo Fortress. After you've gained the Gerudo Pass and can freely explore the fortress, make your way to the back rooftops. Go east along the roof until you reach a gap that's too large to jump. Play the Scarecrow Song to summon him across the gap, and then use the Longshot to pull yourself across. Inside the chest will be a Piece of Heart.

It's time to put those archery skills to the ultimate test. For this Piece of Heart, after you earned the Gerudo Pass, go to the southeastern corner of Gerudo Fortress. Summon Epona and talk to the woman under the awning. She will explain that they have a mini-game to see how many points you can earn. Your goal is to get 1,000 points in a single run. The simpletest way to do this is to hit 10 bullseyes (red circles), as these reward 100 points each. Once you get over 1,000 points, you'll get this Piece of Heart.

Our last Piece of Heart can be found in the Evil Desert Colossus. After you learn the Requiem of Spirit from Sheik, return to the Temple of Time and become Young Link. Then play the song to return to the Spirit Temple exterior. Right outside the door to the left, will be a bug hole you can plant a Magic Bean into. Once you do, come back to this location as Adult Link and ride the Magic Bean Flower through the area until it stops right in front of a Piece of Heart.

Nintendo has only gone and done it again.

#4242. Old School RuneScape lets you test your mettle with the introduction of Hardcore Worlds

Old School RuneScape and the whole RuneScape-verse has been going for nigh-on 20 years now, and for those looking for a challenge, there are plenty of bosses and dungeons to face. But now, even the most experienced of players can face a true trial, as today, Hardcore Worlds arrive in Old School RuneScape on all platforms, mobile included.

Hardcore Worlds function exactly as you'd expect them to, but if you're new to the concept, here's a brief explainer: In Hardcore Worlds, death is final. As in no retries, no restarts. Whether it's slow or sudden, if your character perishes, you can either discard them or transfer them to a regular server, though without the rewards or goodies available exclusively on Hardcore Worlds.

And if you're curious about stepping in and giving Hardcore Worlds a go, now's a good time! Because from today, Reaper's Raffle and World First rewards will allow you to win real-world prizes by completing tasks for the Reaper. Accomplishing tasks enters you into a raffle, with plenty of exciting goodies on offer for those who step into the Hardcore worlds.

Off the back of the Road to Restoration, it seemed as if Jagex faced a stumbling block with the community rejection of RuneScape: Reignited. But if the introduction of Hardcore Worlds is any indication, they still have plenty of crowd-pleasers up their sleeve.

Still, while Old School RuneScape is undoubtedly an exciting, storied MMORPG for many fans, there's always something new vying for the spotlight. Just take a look at our list of the best mobile games of 2026 (so far) for some of our choice picks!

#4241. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

#4239. App Army Assemble: Crushed In Time - "Is this comedic point-and-click adventure a must-play?"

Crushed In Time is yet another point-and-click adventure from the folks behind There Is No Game: Wrong Dimension. Given that our App Army is familiar with the team's previous work, we decided to ask them if Draw Me A Pixel's latest effort is worth playing.

Crushed In Time is a beautifully animated cartoon-style adventure following the iconic duo of Sherlock Holmes and Dr John Watson. While the game falls into the traditional point-and-click genre, you’ll actually be using a rather fun “catch and stretch” mechanic that works really well on your touchscreen device. The presentation is all top-notch, everything looks simply gorgeous, and the excellent dialogue is superbly voice-acted, keeping you glued to the screen throughout.

The puzzles here can get challenging at times; I often found myself resorting to some trial and error. Luckily, there’s a really nice hint system that’s available to alleviate any difficulties you may run into, which you can use at your discretion. I loved my time spent with Crushed In Time - two thumbs up!

This is a fun point-and-click adventure. The cartoon graphics are appealing. The stretch and release system is unique and adds to the atmosphere; the occasional fourth-wall breaking and British humour make it fun. Fun enough to make up for the initial frustration.

I needed the hint system a lot early on, but less as I started to get the groove of the game. And yeah, I’m pretty much always up for some time travel hills. In an App Store full of point-and-click games (that I’m honestly not a huge fan of, mostly because I’m not always good at them?) This one rises above the pack thanks to its relentless fun and humour. Definitely worth trying for free.

I was expecting a point-and-click adventure, and then I noticed the developers are the same ones responsible for the There Is No Game game. And that's how we get a very ingenious slingshot-and-click game instead of a classic point-and-click. So, the fourth wall breaks in this Sherlock Holmes reimagination adventure with some time travel added to the mix, where we need to stretch everything and every object on screen to make things happen or move. Our heroes feel that something paranormal is happening around them (shhh, don't tell them—it's our hand doing the paranormal stuff, the hand of God). With a lot of humour everywhere, you can see the characters complaining for something to happen.

Then, we make it happen by stretching something or activating an object by means of rotation, and they will take credit for whatever happened. The puzzles are fun to solve, and there's a hint system in place if you don't like to rely on trial and error so much. A lot of physics is involved in how we manipulate objects and people to make things happen. I must say I'm having a lot of fun with this game. The mechanics and controls are very innovative; the voice acting and humour are superb, as are the graphics, animations, and the Indiana Jones-like soundtrack. There aren't a lot of games like this one, that's for sure. If you're into point-and-click games, or just games completely outside the box, this one is surely for you.

Crushed in Time is a good-looking point-and-click adventure. A game within a game, as a mysterious letter sends Holmes and Watson on a journey. The novelty here is that you manipulate the characters and objects by stretching and releasing areas of the screen. The cartoon graphics and voice acting are good, and there is an excellent hint system. The stretching mechanic can be frustrating at times; it took me a while just to wake up Holmes at the start. Recommended if you like this type of game.

Crushed in Time is overall brilliant and unique in terms of controls, as things work with elastic controls (instead of tap or button control, we have to grab, pull, and release). I love the comedic theme, superb writing and voiceovers. The puzzles work like magic, especially because of those unique controls. Cartoon graphics work like charm, and also a shout-out for giving amazing animation work when we interact with the world in the game.

Crushed in Time is a fourth-wall-breaking British humour puzzle where the linear adventure game approach with all of its typical crazy inventory combinations is replaced by physics-based gameplay and some tricky timing combos too. The conceit is that the game developers have lost control of their code, so the in-game characters must traverse the program and save the day by setting the environment to rights.

Does it work? Yes... and no. The generous use of “point-and-click game logic” often means you’ll rely on a great deal of trial and error (or the hint system) to find the exact solution dreamed up by a specific developer rather than something you think should work. While that’s typical of p&c games in general, it’s doubled down on here due to the stretch-and-release game mechanic, which works better on a touch screen than on a computer.

Beautiful graphics, inventive approach to puzzle solving (which fails as often as it succeeds), silly humour, good music and voice work all add up to something worth trying. Fortunately, there’s a lengthy demo if you want to try before buying. The full game runs about 6 hours of playtime. Recommended if you can stand frustration. Best in short bursts. To join, simply head over to either our Discord Channel or Facebook Group and request access by answering the three questions. We'll then get you in right away.

#4238. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

#4237. Here's The Best Graphics And Performance Mode For Phantom Blade Zero On PlayStation 5

Phantom Blade Zero is out now for everyone as a console exclusive on PlayStation 5 and on PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store as well. If you missed it, it's my favorite action game of the year so far, and you can read why in Game Informer's Phantom Blade Zero review. That explains why I think you should check the game out; Game Informer's list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks will get you some key information I wish I had when I started the game; and this guide I wrote up about the requirements you need to get the best ending in Phantom Blade Zero will help you find all story-critical content in the game.

However, you're looking for advice on which of the three visual modes Phantom Blade Zero offers you should use on your PS5. This here piece is for you.

Phantom Blade Zero has three visual modes on PS5 Pro: Quality, Balanced, and Performance. I tested all three. My personal favorite was Balanced, which gives you an upscaled (checkerboarded) 4K resolution at 40 FPS, as long as you have a 120Hz TV with VRR. If you have a 120Hz TV, it likely has VRR because most major manufacturers include it with 120Hz. I like this mode because the upscaled 4K looks beautiful, just a hair less than native 4K, and if you aren't someone super trained on those details, I'd wager you won't notice the difference. The best part is that this mode offers 40 FPS gameplay, which, contrary to how math works, is halfway between 30 FPS and 60 FPS; I'm not kidding, look it up. As such, 40 FPS feels much smoother than 30 FPS, and you're still getting crisp 4K resolution. It's a win-win for me and my go-to mode when a game offers it. That said, if you don’t have a PS5 Pro, you won’t see this Balanced mode.

The Performance mode offers an upscaled 2K resolution with a pretty locked 60 FPS. Phantom Blade Zero is an extremely fast, fluid action game, so I think many people will want the buttery smoothness of 60 FPS gameplay. If that's you, pick the Performance mode. Sure, its resolution is lower, and it will look blurrier and less crisp than the other two modes, but if you aren't switching back and forth often or looking at side-by-side images, you likely won't notice.

Quality mode is native 4K resolution (absolutely beautiful, the best visual image you can get playing Phantom Blade Zero), but at 30 FPS... and for a game like this, I don't think 30 FPS does it justice. I don't really recommend this mode for combat, but if you're just waltzing around Wulin, grabbing screenshots and such, turn it on and bask in the wonders of developer S-Game's art team. Note: There is an option for ray tracing on PS5 Pro. I tested all three graphics modes with it on and off and noticed zero performance changes or issues. So, use ray tracing – it’s nice!

#4236. Gunboat God sets November launch date for its crocodile-powered shoot 'em up

Getting home involves shooting just about everything in sight

Your mechanic in Gunboat God is a crocodile called Yeti. I’ve read that back a few times now and it still doesn’t make any more sense, but he’s apparently the best in the trade and a genuinely good guy, so I’ll stop asking questions. He’s heading to iOS and Android with the rest of this side-scrolling shoot ’em up, and to Switch as well.

You’re stuck somewhere you don’t recognise, trying to get back to a Citadel in the sky, and the best thing you’ve got is a boat with an alarming amount of firepower bolted to it. Getting home means going through more than twenty mission types. Collision Course and Outlast explain themselves, while one is just called Boil.

There are eight guns to master, cannons and lasers among them, alongside something called the Vaporiser that I’m choosing to believe isn’t a kettle. Each gets its own upgrades, and there are more than ten abilities and augments for the boat on top.

It transforms mid-level too, diving below the surface or lifting off above it, which helps when there are mines underneath and acid rain overhead. Seventy enemy types and a run of multi-phase bosses stand between you and home, spread over 180 levels.

On mobile, Gunboat God is going the try-before-you-buy route. The first biome is free with no adverts, and you pay to unlock the rest. Premium shoot ’em ups are a hard sell on phones and a free slice should answer most questions directly.

The catch is how far the slice goes. If the first biome ends on one of those multi-phase bosses, you’ll know whether the touch controls keep up once the screen fills with bullets, and that’s the test this genre lives or dies on.

Gunboat God launches on November 17th for iOS and Android.

#4235. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4234. Fragmentary Order Looks Like Sci-Fi Escape from Tarkov, And You Can Play It This Year

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer. The game director behind the popular hardcore shooter has finally offered a proper look at his next project, and it seems he's not planning to make things any easier for players.

Called Fragmentary Order, the upcoming sci-fi tactical shooter just received its first gameplay reveal, featuring an impressive 14 minutes of in-engine footage. And if you're curious to see what Buyanov has been working on, you can watch the full gameplay reveal on YouTube!

Escape From Tarkov's creator reveals that his upcoming game is 'almost there.'

Set across the Solar System in 2251, Fragmentary Order imagines a future where warfare has become an outsourced business. So, instead of putting their own lives on the line, players control remotely operated clones known as RepEnts, which are deployed across large combat zones to carry out all sorts of dangerous missions.

Interestingly, losing one of these clones isn't necessarily the end of the road. In this world, death is simply another business expense, but that doesn't mean players can afford to be careless. The game features large-scale environments, changing environmental conditions, vehicles, drones, and advanced technological systems, with squads of up to four players expected to coordinate their operations.

If you've ever wondered what Escape from Tarkov would look like if its brutal firefights took place somewhere beyond Earth, Nikita Buyanov might have just the answer.

Buyanov is also taking a more grounded approach to its sci-fi setting (as you should expect from the same mind that created Escape From Tarkov). Rather than relying on futuristic gimmicks like wall-hacks, the upcoming hardcore shooter features electromagnetic sensors that can expose players' positions, meaning every encounter requires careful planning and an understanding of the battlefield. In other words, running around without thinking twice probably won't get you very far!

Battlestate Games boss Nikita Buyanov opens up about his creative vision for his upcoming game, Fragmentary Order.

Alongside the gameplay reveal, Buyanov also announced “Prime Batch”, a paid program that gives players access to the game's upcoming closed testing sessions. So yes, some dedicated fans won't have to wait until the game's full release to get their hands on it, as closed testing sessions are expected to begin later this year.

There are two available tiers: Candidate ($44.99), which includes access to alpha sessions and major technical playtests, and Founder ($79.99), which adds earlier access to experimental builds, roadmap updates, and a private community with direct developer access. The first closed alpha wave is planned for later this year, and you can check out more about it on this page.

For now, Fragmentary Order doesn't have a confirmed release date, but its first gameplay showcase has certainly given fans plenty to discuss. If Buyanov manages to capture the same long-term appeal that made Escape from Tarkov so popular while introducing a compelling sci-fi setting, his next project could be one worth keeping an eye on.

Fragmentary Order is a next-generation multiplayer combat tactical simulator.

#4233. How To Complete The Great Deku Tree Dungeon In The Ocarina Of Time Remake

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has finally been released, so grab your bottle of milk, load up your bomb pouch, and get ready to set off on one of gaming's most beloved adventures. Along this journey, you will encounter multiple large dungeons which make up a large portion of the story's challenge.

The first dungeon you will need to complete is the Great Deku Tree. If you're struggling to beat this or just want to know where all the Gold Skulltulas are located, here is how to fully complete this dungeon and find everything inside it.

Upon entering the Great Deku Tree, you will find yourself inside the main trunk of this being. In the middle of the floor is a large spider web. Around the perimeter of this room are various bushes and a new enemy: the Deku Baba. Unlike the version you encountered making your way to the Great Deku Tree, these will lash out at you. Use your shield to block and then strike them a couple of times to kill them.

Make a mental note of the spider web for now and head to the wall of vines. Climb up the vines, jump across the gap, and approach the large treasure chest. Inside you will find the Dungeon Map, which you can use to orientate yourself and see what areas you haven't visited. Continue up the path around the main chamber and go through the stone door.

Inside, you will encounter a Deku Scrub who hides underground whenever you get close. To defeat this enemy, hold up your shield and wait for it to spit a Deku Nut. This will bounce off the shield and ricochet back to the Scrub, knocking him from the ground. Rush over and slash at him a few times to trigger a brief dialogue exchange. He will explain that you can break your fall if you jump from a high place by holding forward.

I want them all, but that will require buying multiple copies of the game in various countries.

After beating the Deku Scrub, head through the door behind him to enter the next room. Inside, you will see another large treasure chest at the end of a large broken branch. Run across the branch to have it break apart under your feet, dropping Link to the floor below. Climb up the vines on either side to reach the chest, which contains the Fairy Slingshot.

Equip the slingshot by holding down R and then highlighting this weapon. Now, turn and face the Skullwalltula on the vines and lock onto it with Navi. Fire the slingshot at the enemy to kill it, climb the vines, and open the chest to receive a Rupee.

Jump back down to where you opened the chest and look at the way you initially entered the room. Above the door will be an eye, so hold down the right trigger to manually aim the slingshot and fire it at the eye. This will cause it to close and drop a stone ladder to the ground that can be used to return to the main chamber.

Once you're back in the main room, head to where you found the Dungeon Map, and use the slingshot to kill the three Skullwalltulas on the vines above the chest. If you don't, these Skullwalltulas will attack and knock you off the vines if you try to climb by them. With the enemies dead, go up the vines until you reach the next floor.

Head to the door, but don't just rush in, as a large Skulltula will fall from the ceiling. To kill this enemy, approach it until it starts to shake, and then quickly back up before it performs a spin attack. Wait until the Skulltula slows down and attack its glowing blue underbelly. Repeat this twice to kill this enemy, allowing you to access the room inside.

Go into the Compass Room and step on the stone switch to your right. This will cause three platforms in the center to temporarily rise up. Jump across them to the other side of the room where the chest is. To the left of the chest will be a Deku Baba, so kill it and then open the chest to obtain the Compass.

Now, move behind the chest, cut the grass, and climb through the crawl space to reach a hidden room. Go up the vines to find a small chest with a Rupee in it. Head back to the main Compass Room and go to the door you entered from to return to the main chamber.

The first Gold Skulltula in this dungeon can be found in the Compass Room. Before hitting the stone switch, jump down and head to the left side of the room. A Skulltula will drop from the ceiling, so kill it and then climb back up to where the switch is. Step on it to raise the stone platforms, go across them, and head to the opening on the left. Slash at the golden arachnid on the wall to earn your first Skultula Token.

Back in the main chamber, upon exiting the Compass Room, head left up the path. There will be two more Skulltulas you'll need to deal with until you reach the top. You'll find a part where a branch sticks out a bit over the main floor. Walk onto the branch and look down at the spider web. To reach the lower level, you will need to jump from where you are standing to the spider web below.

Doing so will cause the web to break, dropping you into the lower level. I recommend making sure you have gotten all the items and Gold Skulltula before doing this; otherwise, you will need to climb back up via a long vine wall, which is fairly tedious. When you reach the lower floor, climb out of the water, and head right towards the stone switch and unlit torch.

After landing in the water from falling through the spider web, turn immediately around and face the large vine wall leading back up to the first floor. On the vines will be a Gold Skulltula you can kill via the Fairy Slingshot. Hit it once, climb the vines, and grab your second token.

To the left of the stone switch will be another Gold Skulltula on some metal bars. Shoot it with your slingshot and then jump from the stone platform to reach the floating token.

With those two Gold Skulltulas acquired, step onto the stone switch next to the until torch to ignite it and burn away the spider web. Open the small chest to get some Deku Sticks and then equip one. Pull out a Deku Stick by hitting the Right Trigger and approach the torch with the stick to ignite it. Quickly, run across the stone platforms to the spider web covering the door and touch the burning stick to the web.

This will burn it away, allowing you to access the next room. Head inside and use your shield to dislodge the Deku Scrub. Run over to it and whack away at this enemy until it surrenders. The Deku Scrub will explain that you cannot defeat his siblings unless you deflect their projectiles in a specific order, which is 2-3-1. Use the Fairy Slingshot to shoot the eye over the barred door to unlock it and head into the next room.

In the next room there will be a moving platform going across the water that slides under a rotating spike log. To get past this trap, go into the water and dive down in the left corner to press an underwater stone switch. This will cause the water level to temporarily lower, so quickly climb back up to where you entered. Jump onto the platform and ride it, as you will now be low enough that you will pass right under the spiked log.

Go through the door to enter the next room and kill the Skultula that drops from the ceiling. After it's dead, move to the left of the large stone block and grab onto it with A. Push the block until it cannot be moved anymore and then climb up it to reach the door to the next room. Kill all the Deku Babas around the torch and then equip a Deku Stick. Use the stick to light the three unlit torches in each corner of the room to unlock the door.

When you go into the next room, you will be attacked by the Skulltula right as you enter. Once it's dead, a Gohma Larva will drop from the ground and hatch. Hold up your shield and wait for this enemy to launch itself at you. Block with the shield to stun it before swinging your sword. Once it's dead, look up at the ceiling, equip your slingshot, and shoot the two remaining Gohma Larva eggs to kill them before they drop to the ground and attack.

Gold Skulltula 4 Location — Gohma Larva Room (B1)

The fourth Gold Skulltula is located in the same room where you encountered the three Gohma Larvas. Take out the Deku Stick and burn away the spider web on the left via the torch. This will let you access the side room. Inside, kill the big Skulltula that drops from the ceiling, before using your slingshot to slay the Gold Skulltula on the vines. Climb up the vines to get the next Skulltula Token.

With the Gohma Larva dead, use your Deku Stick to burn away the spider web blocking the path to the right to proceed through the crawlspace. This will spit you back out into the lower main chamber, so approach the stone block and push it towards the water. This will cause it to drop and create a shortcut to where the ignited torch is located.

Equip your Deku Stick and head over to the torch. Light the stick and make your way back up the stone block to where the spider web on the ground is. Swing the lit Deku Stick while on the spider web by hitting ZR to burn it away. You will then fall into the water below and reach the lowest level of this dungeon.

Approach the three Deku Scrubs, but do not just block and attack each one. You need to ricochet their seeds back in a specific order, which was told to you earlier in the dungeon. The correct order you need to stun the Deku Scrubs is 2-3-1, with one being on the left and three being on the right. Once you block all the shots in the correct order, smack the remaining Deku Scrub with your sword.

This will cause him to give up, unlock the door, and leave a Rupee for your troubles. Equip the Fairy Slingshot and head inside the boss room.

Goham is the first boss of Ocarina of Time and, unsurprisingly, she's fairly easy to actually beat.

To start the fight, when you enter the room, look up at her glowing eye on the ceiling. Doing so will trigger a brief cutscene where she drops from the ceiling and begins the boss fight. When it starts, Gohma will protect her glowing eye with her mandibles while she follows you around the arena.

Upon getting close, she will raise both of her large limbs and then slam them down in front of her. Once the limbs go up, step back and wait for her to miss this attack. This will cause her to briefly become stunned, making her eye glow green, which is your signal to rush over and attack Gohma with your sword. After getting hit, she will retreat up the wall.

Equip your Fairy Slingshot as she climbs onto the ceiling and wait for her to stop moving. Aim the slingshot at her eye and shoot it to stun the boss and send her plummeting to the floor. Gohma will lie there for several seconds, so run over and start hacking away at her until she recovers and uses her mandibles to block her eye once more.

If you're not fast enough to take Gohma down from the ceiling, she will produce several Gohma Larvae that will join her in this fight. If this happens, prioritize the larva before refocusing on the boss.

You will then need to repeat this same process above at least two more times. Make sure to always wait until you hear the audio cue from Gohma when her limbs are raised, as this indicates she is committing to her frontal attack, and you can backflip away. If you run away too soon, she will not attempt to strike you.

Gohma will have no additional attacks or changes during this fight, so keep up the rhythm of baiting out her strikes and shooting her down from the ceiling until she is killed. You can now pick up the Heart Container to gain a full additional heart and complete this dungeon.

Dark Link is even more of an aura farmer than ever before in the Ocarina of Time remake.

#4231. A Fool's Errand is a one-dimensional climber where your ascent is measured in swipes

It seems rather fitting that just earlier I was writing up my review for Titanium Court (see it soon!) and this crossed my desk. Once an inhabitant of the Playdate platform, A Fool's Errand has unexpectedly become available for purchase on iOS. But, what exactly makes this game such a natural fit for mobile?

Well, as you might expect A Fool's Errand was originally set to make use of the Playdate's signature crank, which would manage how fast your humble hero Roland ascended the sinister staircase. You used the crank to ascend, dodging traps and enemies as you went. So with only a single means of control it certainly isn't losing anything by jumping to mobile.

I'd have to see how it plays in practice, but it's interesting to see A Fool's Errand make the jump from the platform it was tailor-made for to iOS. Given the Playdate was always a bit of a niche device, that's to be expected, but how well it translates to more imprecise swiping controls will change how well it plays. But at the same time it has the atmosphere to carry itself despite that.

Certainly, the most gripping thing about A Fool's Errand is how it looks. So if you fancy a simple but engaging puzzler and dark, moody monochrome graphics, then it may well be worth giving A Fool's Errand a look to see what it offers! Especially at only $2.99 a pop.

But, if you're looking for more typical dungeon-crawling fare, then don't go smashing your phone just yet. Instead, just dig into our list of the best RPGs on iOS for some other adventures through dank, winding caverns full of treasure and monsters.

#4230. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4229. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

While development of "The Duskbloods" is at the final adjustment stage, we have made the decision to move the launch window to 2027. #4227. Epic Adds Features to Fortnite Crew Subscription, Removes Others

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

Fortnite’s self-perpetuating freemium economy is built around several forms of transactions and subscriptions. The most prominent of these are the Item Shop, where you buy cosmetics piecemeal for V-Bucks, and the Battle Pass, which you buy once per season to gain access to a set sequence of unlockables by leveling up.

In addition to these, though, Fortnite also offers the Fortnite Crew subscription service which, for a recurring monthly fee, gets you access to the current Battle Pass, other content passes like the OG Pass, Music Pass, and for fans of video game LEGO kits, the LEGO Pass, plus a monthly payout of 800 V-Bucks. It costs more than the Battle Pass by itself, but all the extra content is very attractive, especially if you don’t already have a bunch of skins to flip through.

During the Treasure Hunters event, players have a chance to uncover a token that gives near-unfettered access to the item shop for two weeks.

As Epic Games announced on the official Fortnite news blog today, though, some changes are coming to the Crew Subscription starting on December 5. Some of these changes are additive, and may help to improve the value of the subscription gameplay-wise, but they’re accompanied by some subtractions, which could harm the overall bang-for-buck depending on your perspective.

Let’s start with the good news. Firstly, the price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly, and you’ll still get access to the current Battle Pass, Music Pass, LEGO Pass and Rocket Pass Premium.

The price of Fortnite Crew is staying the same at $11.99 monthly.

The people gave Sweeney and Epic all the attention and support it needed when it rose up to Apple. As a reward, players got a significant price hike.

In addition, all Crew members will begin receiving a flat 20% bonus to all XP earned while playing the game, with a 10% XP bonus also given to any squad members in your party, even if they’re not Crew members themselves. These boosts don’t stack, though, so you won’t get any additional XP even if you have other Crew members in your squad.

So, that’s the good news, now what’s the bad news? The first piece of bad news is that Crew Pack Outfits, one of the most distinctive benefits to getting a Crew sub, are being discontinued. The final Crew Pack Outfit will be distributed in December, with no further packs to follow. On the bright side, if there were any Legacy Styles you didn’t have for your Crew Pack Outfits, which would normally be obtained by staying subbed for sequential months, they’ll instead just be given to you in bulk.

The second piece of bad news is that, at least for the time being, OG Pass is ending, with an apparent “dramatic conclusion” occurring on December 5 with the end of Chapter 1: OG Season X. This means you won’t be able to redeem the large quantity of skins and other assorted cosmetics that this pass would normally provide.

That’s definitely a big blow to the overall value factor of a Crew subscription, though according to Epic’s news post, “The Next Era of Fortnite OG drops in late 2027,” so perhaps the OG Pass will make a comeback at some point.

#4225. Assassin’s Creed Franchise Update Reveals Codename Hexe News Coming Next Year, New Game Plus for Valhalla, And Confirms No New Remakes

Ubisoft has released a fall update on the Assassin’s Creed franchise, providing news big and small on its flagship series. The news includes updates for existing games and smaller but significant insights on the various upcoming Assassin’s Creed games previously announced.

In terms of current games, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is getting a long-requested New Game Plus thanks to a new update coming on November 5. This means you can start a fresh game while bringing over your progression items/level from your previous playthrough. This update will also introduce the following features:

This news comes a few days after New Game Plus arrived in Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.

Codname Invictis, a PvP multiplayer game, remains in development as Ubisoft shares it has incorporated feedback from players who, according to Ubisoft, “saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed.” To this end, Ubisoft has spent months reworking Invictis to reflect this vague feedback and say the game is “now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions.”

As for the next single-player Assassin’s Creed, Codename Hexe, Ubisoft says it will share the next major update on this game in 2027. First announced in 2022, Codename Hexe is set during the 17th-century reign of the Holy Roman Empire, and the era's witch hunts will play a significant role.

With the release of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this year, Ubisoft has given fans what they'll likely see as a disappointing update on potential future remakes: “One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development. Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories.”

However, Ubisoft adds that this door isn’t closed for good. “Like many of you, we love the idea of revisiting our classic titles, and we'll keep exploring opportunities to bring older titles back,” says Ubisoft.

Ubisoft’s next update concerns the live-action Assassin's Creed series in production for Netflix. They say the show is “nearing completion” in Rome and that award-winning composer Hannah Peel (Insomnia, Rogue Agent, Game of Thrones: The Last Watch) is composing the score.

Lastly, Ubisoft teases big celebrations are planned for 2027, which marks the 20th anniversary of the Assassin's Creed franchise. It's keeping details to itself for now, but states it's "preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments. "
